background_texts: A former municipal cartographer from Porto, Portugal, this soldier spent the early occupation updating ADVENT transit maps for the city's infrastructure authority. While surveying a restricted underground station, they discovered several sealed platforms being used to transport unwilling human test subjects. After secretly copying the transport schedules, they fled the city and passed the information to a resistance courier. Their knowledge of urban infrastructure subsequently earned them a position with an XCOM reconnaissance unit.

Before the invasion, this soldier worked as a commercial beekeeper in the rural outskirts of Christchurch, New Zealand. ADVENT's agricultural restructuring program eventually displaced independent producers, forcing them to sell their equipment and relocate. Rather than accept reassignment to an automated farming collective, they established an unauthorized apiary in the surrounding hills. A resistance patrol discovered the settlement while searching for food supplies and recruited them after learning they had been sabotaging ADVENT agricultural shipments.

A former emergency room physician from Casablanca, Morocco, this soldier initially accepted an ADVENT medical position believing the occupation authorities could provide desperately needed resources. Their opinion changed when they discovered that patients exhibiting unusual neurological symptoms were being transferred to an undisclosed research facility. After helping several patients escape, they abandoned their position and began treating resistance fighters in a makeshift clinic. An XCOM medical officer eventually encountered them while coordinating an evacuation.

This soldier had worked as a marine engine technician in the coastal communities of western Norway before ADVENT consolidated control of the region. Their familiarity with older vessels made them useful to independent fishing communities operating beyond regular surveillance. When an ADVENT patrol began confiscating boats suspected of transporting refugees, they sabotaged the harbor's automated identification system. A local resistance organization subsequently arranged their transfer to an XCOM supply network.

Originally a competitive fencing instructor from Lyon, France, this soldier struggled to find employment after ADVENT replaced most independent sporting institutions with government-sponsored recreational programs. They eventually became an equipment handler at a regional training facility, where they secretly preserved banned historical sporting manuals. When an ADVENT officer ordered the destruction of the collection, they attacked the facility's security personnel and escaped with several dissidents. Their physical conditioning and unusual combat instincts attracted the attention of a nearby resistance cell.

A former railway signal operator from Plovdiv, Bulgaria, this soldier spent the occupation maintaining an aging freight junction under ADVENT supervision. Their position allowed them to recognize irregular shipments moving through the network, including transports that never appeared on official schedules. After discovering that several neighboring communities had disappeared following similar shipments, they began secretly redirecting freight away from ADVENT facilities. A resistance contact eventually approached them with an offer to provide their knowledge to XCOM.

This soldier had been a professional wildlife photographer working in the forests of British Columbia when the invasion began. As ADVENT expanded its presence into remote regions, they continued documenting animal migration patterns and abandoned settlements. During one expedition, they captured images of a Faceless infiltrating a refugee encampment. Unable to convince local authorities of the discovery, they delivered the evidence to a resistance radio operator. XCOM subsequently recruited them for their fieldcraft and exceptional observation skills.

Before the occupation, this soldier worked as a stage lighting technician in Buenos Aires, Argentina. ADVENT's cultural authorities eventually took control of the city's theaters, transforming several venues into propaganda centers. They continued working behind the scenes until they discovered that the building's maintenance tunnels were being used to detain political dissidents. Using their familiarity with the electrical systems, they disabled the security grid long enough for several prisoners to escape. One of the survivors later introduced them to an XCOM recruitment officer.

A former insurance investigator from Rotterdam, Netherlands, this soldier initially benefited from the occupation's apparent economic stability. Their work involved examining property claims and documenting damage caused by resistance activity. While investigating a suspicious industrial accident, they discovered that ADVENT had deliberately destroyed an entire residential block to conceal an unauthorized alien excavation. They copied the evidence and attempted to expose the incident through underground channels. When their investigation attracted ADVENT attention, a resistance network arranged their extraction and eventual recruitment by XCOM.

This soldier grew up in a family of traveling circus performers in northern Italy, developing considerable skill with acrobatics, animal handling, and improvised equipment. After ADVENT restrictions made public performances increasingly difficult, they joined a small traveling entertainment group operating between isolated settlements. When a Muton patrol confiscated the group's vehicles, they escaped through a maintenance structure too narrow for the aliens to follow. A resistance scout encountered them several days later and recognized their potential for infiltration work.

Formerly a freshwater fisheries inspector in Manitoba, Canada, this soldier spent the occupation monitoring the lakes and rivers surrounding several isolated communities. ADVENT environmental agencies repeatedly dismissed reports of unexplained contamination near restricted facilities. After finding unusual biological material in a tributary, they began collecting samples and distributing warnings to nearby settlements. Their research eventually reached an underground scientific network, which arranged a meeting with XCOM personnel interested in investigating alien waste disposal operations.

This soldier had worked as a watchmaker in Prague, Czech Republic, before ADVENT occupation authorities centralized the city's manufacturing industry. Their small workshop survived by repairing mechanical devices that no longer had replacement parts. When an ADVENT inspection team began confiscating unregistered equipment, they discovered that several supposedly defective security components had been deliberately manufactured with hidden vulnerabilities. Rather than report the discovery, they began supplying modified parts to local dissidents. Their technical knowledge eventually brought them into contact with an XCOM engineering cell.

A former school bus driver from the rural districts of Alberta, this soldier spent the early occupation transporting children between scattered settlements. ADVENT eventually introduced centralized education facilities, requiring families to send their children to government-controlled boarding schools. Concerned by the disappearance of several pupils, they began keeping unofficial records of student transfers. After uncovering evidence of unexplained removals, they redirected an entire bus convoy to a resistance safehouse. The operation brought them to the attention of an XCOM liaison.

Before the invasion, this soldier worked as an archaeological conservator in Alexandria, Egypt, specializing in the restoration of damaged historical artifacts. ADVENT authorities later appropriated the museum collections, claiming that ancient human history was being incorporated into a unified cultural archive. They refused to surrender several privately held excavation records documenting underground structures beneath the city. When security forces raided their workshop, they escaped with the records and sought assistance from a local resistance organization. XCOM recruited them after discovering their knowledge of underground access routes.

This soldier had spent most of their adult life as a competitive long-distance cyclist in the Netherlands. Following the occupation, organized sporting events became increasingly controlled, and independent competitions were prohibited. They turned to courier work, transporting medicine and communications between resistance sympathizers in neighboring districts. During one delivery, an ADVENT checkpoint discovered their concealed cargo, forcing them to escape across a flooded industrial canal. A resistance commander subsequently offered them permanent employment, eventually transferring them to an XCOM mobility unit.

A former industrial chemist from Kaunas, Lithuania, this soldier was employed at an ADVENT-approved materials processing facility during the early occupation. Their responsibilities involved monitoring chemical waste and maintaining production standards. After noticing that unusual compounds were being diverted into shipments marked for agricultural use, they conducted an independent analysis and discovered traces of experimental alien compounds. Their supervisor attempted to have them detained for unauthorized testing. They escaped with their research and eventually found protection within an underground resistance laboratory.

Originally a lighthouse keeper on the coast of Maine, this soldier continued maintaining an isolated navigation station after ADVENT abandoned much of the surrounding maritime infrastructure. The station's remote location made it useful to smugglers and refugee transports. When an ADVENT patrol began using the lighthouse's communications equipment to track unauthorized vessels, they secretly modified its transmitter to broadcast false coordinates. A resistance maritime network discovered the deception and recruited them to assist with coastal operations supporting XCOM.

This soldier had been employed as a professional interpreter in Geneva, Switzerland, working with international relief organizations before the occupation. ADVENT later recruited them to translate communications between regional administrators and alien personnel. During a routine assignment, they recognized inconsistencies in translated detention records that suggested entire communities were being relocated without authorization. They began leaking corrected documents to humanitarian contacts before disappearing from their government position. A resistance intelligence officer eventually arranged their recruitment into an XCOM communications team.

A former coal miner from the Silesian industrial region of Poland, this soldier possessed extensive knowledge of abandoned tunnels and underground ventilation systems. After ADVENT closed several traditional mines, they found temporary employment maintaining automated extraction facilities. An equipment failure trapped a maintenance crew underground, and their attempts to request assistance were deliberately ignored by the facility's supervisors. They organized an escape through an obsolete ventilation shaft, eventually leading the survivors to an underground settlement. Resistance representatives later recruited them for their knowledge of subterranean terrain.

Before joining the resistance, this soldier operated a small independent radio repair shop in Cebu, Philippines. During the occupation, they increasingly specialized in restoring obsolete receivers that ADVENT communications networks could not easily monitor. One customer brought them a damaged transmitter containing fragments of an encrypted resistance broadcast. Curious, they repaired the device and began monitoring its traffic. After inadvertently establishing contact with an XCOM communications operator, they were invited to join a regional resistance network and assist with maintaining clandestine radio equipment.

This soldier was formerly a veterinary surgeon in the rural communities of County Cork, Ireland. They continued treating livestock after ADVENT introduced genetically modified agricultural stock and restricted access to conventional veterinary medicine. When several animals developed identical neurological symptoms, they traced the condition to a nearby water distribution facility. Their investigation revealed that the facility was disposing of biological waste from an alien research installation. After sharing the evidence with local dissidents, they were recruited by a resistance medical team interested in their knowledge of alien-related biological contamination.

A former professional locksmith from Osaka, Japan, this soldier had spent years specializing in obsolete mechanical security systems. ADVENT's transition to centralized electronic identification initially left their profession obsolete, but they continued receiving private requests from people attempting to secure unregistered properties. When a group of dissidents became trapped inside an abandoned administrative building, they were hired to bypass its original security mechanisms. Their successful extraction attracted the attention of a resistance organizer, who subsequently introduced them to XCOM.

This soldier had worked as a commercial airline meteorologist in Santiago, Chile, before ADVENT imposed strict controls over civilian aviation. Their employment continued briefly as part of an atmospheric monitoring program, where they noticed unusual weather patterns surrounding restricted alien installations. After an ADVENT supervisor ordered the deletion of several observation records, they copied the data and contacted an independent research collective. XCOM later recruited them after determining that their atmospheric analysis could help identify concealed alien facilities.

Formerly a furniture restorer in Florence, Italy, this soldier spent the occupation repairing valuable pieces confiscated from private collections and transferred to ADVENT administrators. Their work provided access to restricted government residences, where they occasionally overheard conversations concerning planned security operations. When they discovered that an upcoming raid would target a nearby refugee shelter, they secretly warned its occupants. The survivors established contact with a resistance cell, which later recruited them as an intelligence source and occasional field operative.

This soldier grew up working aboard their family's commercial fishing trawler in the waters surrounding Iceland. Following the invasion, ADVENT restricted independent fishing activity and introduced automated monitoring stations along major shipping routes. They continued operating outside approved waters, transporting medical supplies and escaped prisoners between isolated coastal communities. During one voyage, their vessel was intercepted by an ADVENT patrol, but they escaped through a narrow fjord known only to local fishermen. An XCOM naval liaison subsequently recruited them for maritime reconnaissance duties.

A former accountant from Accra, Ghana, this soldier had been responsible for managing the finances of several small manufacturing cooperatives. Under ADVENT's economic restructuring program, their employers were absorbed into a centralized production authority. They were retained to reconcile inventory records and eventually noticed repeated discrepancies involving shipments of military equipment. Their investigation revealed a network of collaborators diverting supplies for personal profit. Rather than expose the arrangement through official channels, they passed the evidence to a resistance contact, who recruited them as a logistics specialist.

Before the occupation, this soldier worked as an elevator maintenance technician in Seoul, South Korea. Their expertise in high-rise infrastructure allowed them to continue working after ADVENT took control of the city's residential towers. During a routine repair, they discovered an unauthorized access route connecting several buildings to a hidden detention facility. They used the route to help a group of prisoners escape, disabling multiple security systems in the process. One of the rescued individuals later introduced them to an XCOM urban operations team.

This soldier had been a professional ice sculptor in Helsinki, Finland, producing elaborate installations for seasonal festivals. ADVENT's cultural restrictions eventually eliminated most independent artistic commissions, forcing them into temporary refrigeration maintenance work. Their new employment brought them into contact with a government storage facility containing unidentified biological specimens. After witnessing an improperly secured specimen escape its container, they triggered an evacuation and helped prevent the contamination from spreading. A resistance scientific cell later recruited them for their knowledge of industrial cooling systems.

A former court stenographer from Edinburgh, Scotland, this soldier spent the early occupation transcribing legal proceedings under ADVENT-appointed judges. They gradually noticed that verdicts were being prepared before defendants were formally charged, with evidence routinely fabricated to justify predetermined sentences. After secretly preserving several transcripts, they began distributing copies through underground legal networks. When their activities were discovered, a resistance group helped them escape the city. XCOM eventually recruited them to assist with interrogation records and intelligence documentation.

This soldier had worked as a high-altitude construction supervisor in the Andes of Peru, overseeing remote infrastructure projects before the invasion. ADVENT later employed them to coordinate maintenance crews working on a communications relay station. During construction, they discovered that the station's foundations concealed an older human research facility that had been sealed without explanation. After finding surviving records indicating unauthorized human experimentation, they abandoned the project and contacted local dissidents. Their engineering experience and knowledge of mountain installations made them a valuable XCOM recruit.

Formerly a professional puppeteer from Kraków, Poland, this soldier continued performing small private shows after ADVENT restricted independent entertainment. Their traveling performances allowed them to move between communities without attracting much attention. During one show, they recognized an audience member as a missing resistance courier whose disappearance had been publicly announced by ADVENT. They helped the courier evade surveillance by concealing them among their equipment. The courier subsequently introduced them to a resistance network, where their ability to travel unnoticed proved useful for intelligence work.

This soldier had been a commercial greenhouse designer in the Netherlands, specializing in automated irrigation and climate control systems. ADVENT's agricultural policies initially made their expertise highly sought after, but they eventually discovered that several government facilities were cultivating experimental plants using alien biological material. After a containment failure contaminated a nearby settlement's water supply, they secretly disabled the irrigation network to prevent further exposure. Resistance scientists investigating the incident recruited them for their technical knowledge and familiarity with controlled agricultural environments.

A former mountain rescue volunteer from the Swiss Alps, this soldier spent the occupation assisting travelers stranded by increasingly restricted transportation routes. ADVENT eventually classified independent rescue operations as unauthorized movements of civilians. When a group of refugees became trapped during a winter storm, they ignored evacuation orders and led the survivors through an abandoned alpine service tunnel. A resistance patrol encountered the group days later and offered them protection. Their experience navigating dangerous terrain eventually brought them into XCOM's field operations.

This soldier worked as a municipal waste collector in Detroit, Michigan, before ADVENT's industrial restructuring displaced most civilian sanitation crews. They continued working unofficially, collecting discarded machinery and electronic components from abandoned manufacturing districts. While searching a demolished factory, they discovered a hidden cache of resistance equipment that had been buried beneath industrial waste. Instead of selling the materials, they contacted the original owners through an intercepted radio frequency. The resulting connection led to their recruitment as a scavenging and equipment recovery specialist.

Before the invasion, this soldier was a marine biology graduate student conducting research along the coast of Tasmania, Australia. Their studies continued under an ADVENT-sponsored environmental program, although access to certain offshore regions was prohibited. During an unauthorized survey, they discovered an unusual concentration of alien microorganisms near a submerged research structure. When their university supervisor attempted to confiscate the findings, they escaped with the samples. An underground scientific collective subsequently introduced them to XCOM researchers investigating aquatic alien contamination.

A former professional baker from Lyon, France, this soldier operated a neighborhood bakery that survived the occupation by supplying basic food to nearby residents. ADVENT eventually imposed mandatory production quotas, requiring local businesses to provide rations for government facilities. They began quietly reserving surplus ingredients for families unable to obtain official food allocations. When an inspector discovered the practice, they were ordered to identify everyone receiving assistance. Instead, they destroyed the distribution records and fled with the help of a resistance contact who had regularly collected supplies.

This soldier had served as a civilian flight instructor in the rural districts of Montana before ADVENT restricted private aircraft ownership. Their knowledge of older aviation equipment remained valuable to independent pilots operating beyond controlled airspace. After witnessing an ADVENT transport aircraft make an emergency landing near an abandoned airstrip, they discovered several injured human prisoners aboard. They helped the survivors escape before security forces arrived. One of the rescued prisoners was a resistance operative who subsequently arranged their recruitment into an XCOM aviation support network.

Originally employed as a museum security guard in Mexico City, this soldier spent years protecting historical exhibits after ADVENT took control of the institution. Their responsibilities included maintaining surveillance equipment and reporting unauthorized visitors. When a government delegation arrived to remove several artifacts, they discovered that the objects had been concealing a collection of pre-invasion research documents. Rather than allow the records to disappear, they smuggled them out through the museum's maintenance tunnels. A resistance historian later connected them with XCOM intelligence personnel.

A former commercial diver from Split, Croatia, this soldier specialized in underwater repairs to shipping infrastructure. ADVENT initially retained their services to maintain submerged power conduits and communication cables. While working near a restricted coastal installation, they discovered an underwater entrance used by unidentified transport vessels. After documenting the activity, they were pursued by an ADVENT security team and escaped by taking refuge inside a damaged wreck. Their evidence reached a maritime resistance group, which recruited them to investigate alien logistics operations.

This soldier had worked as an independent sign painter in the streets of Mumbai, India, producing advertisements and decorative murals for local businesses. ADVENT's propaganda department eventually offered them steady employment creating government-approved public displays. They accepted the position for financial reasons but began hiding small alterations in their work, directing observant citizens toward underground shelters and resistance contacts. When an ADVENT inspector noticed the pattern, they escaped before their identity could be confirmed. A resistance organizer subsequently recruited them to assist with clandestine communications.

Formerly a professional dog trainer in rural Sweden, this soldier specialized in preparing search animals for wilderness rescue operations. During the occupation, they continued working with privately owned dogs after ADVENT introduced strict licensing requirements. When a local resistance courier disappeared in a forested region, they volunteered to search despite warnings that the area was being monitored by ADVENT patrols. Their dogs located the courier's hidden shelter, allowing the injured operative to survive. The rescue established a connection that eventually led to their recruitment by XCOM.

This soldier had been a hydraulic engineer working on flood defenses in Bangladesh before the invasion. ADVENT's reconstruction projects initially provided employment, but their concerns grew when several drainage systems were deliberately redirected toward unauthorized settlements. After discovering that the changes would flood a district occupied by political detainees, they sabotaged the control mechanisms and opened an alternative evacuation route. A group of displaced residents later connected them with an underground resistance organization, which recognized their value in infrastructure sabotage operations.

A former professional billiards player from Las Vegas, Nevada, this soldier had spent years traveling between private clubs and international competitions. After ADVENT imposed restrictions on independent entertainment venues, they found work as a dealer in a government-approved recreation center. Their access to the establishment's clientele allowed them to overhear information from military contractors and administrative officials. When they learned that a resistance safehouse had been identified, they anonymously passed on the warning. The safehouse commander later offered them a place within the local resistance network.

Before the invasion, this soldier was a traditional textile dyer in Jaipur, India, operating a small workshop inherited from their parents. ADVENT's manufacturing policies threatened independent artisans, but they continued producing fabrics for informal trading networks. Their dyes eventually became useful for marking hidden resistance supply caches with patterns invisible under ordinary inspection. After a shipment was intercepted, they volunteered to personally transport the remaining materials. A resistance quartermaster recognized their reliability and recommended them for an XCOM support position.

This soldier worked as a geological surveyor in the volcanic highlands of Guatemala before ADVENT's occupation. Their assignments involved mapping unstable terrain and identifying safe routes for remote construction teams. While conducting a government-approved survey, they discovered an underground chamber containing equipment that appeared to predate the invasion but had been recently modified with alien technology. When ADVENT personnel attempted to seal the site, they escaped with several geological records. A resistance research group later recruited them to assist in identifying concealed underground installations.

A former professional chess instructor from Belgrade, Serbia, this soldier continued teaching privately after ADVENT prohibited independent educational organizations. Their lessons attracted students from several politically sensitive families, some of whom later disappeared into government custody. Rather than abandon the remaining students, they organized an informal network that passed messages through coded chess problems. One of their students eventually made contact with a resistance intelligence officer, who recognized the network's usefulness. The instructor was subsequently recruited to help XCOM coordinate clandestine information exchanges.

This soldier had worked as a refrigeration mechanic in the industrial ports of Busan, South Korea. During the occupation, they maintained storage systems for ADVENT's regional food distribution centers. Their position allowed them to notice unusual shipments requiring temperatures far below those used for conventional food storage. After discovering human biological samples inside one shipment, they copied its manifest and quietly alerted a resistance contact. When ADVENT investigators began questioning the facility's employees, they disappeared into an underground network and eventually joined XCOM.

Formerly a professional mountain guide in the Carpathian Mountains of Romania, this soldier spent the occupation leading small groups through remote wilderness routes. Their services were initially offered to wealthy individuals seeking to avoid government checkpoints, but they gradually began accepting refugees without payment. During one journey, an ADVENT patrol pursued their group into a narrow mountain pass. They successfully led the refugees through an abandoned shepherd's trail and later encountered a resistance recruitment team. Their extensive knowledge of the region made them a valuable reconnaissance specialist.

This soldier was a former forensic accountant from São Paulo, Brazil, who specialized in identifying financial fraud within large corporations. ADVENT's administrative authorities initially retained their services to audit companies suspected of resisting government restructuring. They discovered that several supposedly private organizations were receiving payments for supplying human subjects to alien research facilities. Unable to expose the scheme through official channels, they assembled a detailed financial record and transmitted it to an underground journalist. The journalist connected them with a resistance intelligence network that eventually transferred them to XCOM.

Before joining the resistance, this soldier worked as a clock tower maintenance specialist in the historic districts of Kyoto, Japan. Their occupation required them to travel between several municipal buildings, many of which had been repurposed by ADVENT. During a routine inspection, they discovered that an old mechanical clock concealed a functioning shortwave transmitter left behind by an earlier resistance cell. After restoring the device, they began receiving messages from isolated survivors seeking assistance. One transmission eventually established contact with an XCOM communications officer, who arranged their recruitment into the resistance.

A former forensic pathologist from Reykjavík, Iceland, this soldier worked in a civilian morgue before ADVENT introduced centralized procedures for handling unexplained deaths. Their responsibilities eventually included examining bodies recovered from restricted government facilities. After discovering that several deceased civilians had undergone identical surgical procedures while still alive, they secretly preserved tissue samples and medical photographs. When an ADVENT investigator began questioning their activities, they escaped through an underground medical supply network and were eventually recruited by an XCOM intelligence officer.

Before the invasion, this soldier operated a small roadside repair garage in the Australian outback, specializing in older diesel vehicles. ADVENT's automated transportation systems initially reduced their workload, but remote settlements continued relying on independent mechanics. When a passing resistance convoy suffered an engine failure near their workshop, they offered repairs without asking questions. An ADVENT patrol arrived during the work, forcing them to help the convoy escape through an abandoned mining road. The resistance group later returned and offered them a permanent position.

A former parliamentary research assistant from Wellington, New Zealand, this soldier had specialized in preparing environmental legislation and public policy reports. Following the invasion, they were retained by an ADVENT administrative office to review historical government documents. Their access to archived records revealed that several supposedly voluntary relocation programs had been planned years in advance of their public announcement. After copying the documents, they anonymously distributed them through underground information channels. A resistance journalist eventually introduced them to XCOM, where their administrative experience proved useful in intelligence analysis.

This soldier had spent most of their life as a professional rodeo competitor in Calgary, Canada. Their career ended when ADVENT prohibited independent sporting events and converted several arenas into military recruitment centers. They found work breaking horses at a remote agricultural settlement, where they became familiar with the surrounding wilderness. When a group of ADVENT deserters attempted to seize the settlement's food supplies, they organized its residents into a successful defense. A resistance patrol subsequently recruited them for their horsemanship, physical endurance, and practical leadership.

Formerly a pediatric dentist in Thessaloniki, Greece, this soldier continued operating a small clinic during the early occupation. Their practice eventually became a refuge for families unable to access ADVENT-approved medical services. During one examination, they discovered an unusual implant embedded in a young patient's jaw, apparently inserted during an undocumented medical procedure. Their attempts to investigate the implant attracted the attention of government officials. A resistance medical team helped them escape the city and later arranged their transfer to XCOM's medical division.

This soldier had worked as a professional cave surveyor in the limestone regions of northern Vietnam. After ADVENT restricted access to several natural underground formations, they continued exploring abandoned cave systems for independent scientific clients. During an expedition, they discovered a hidden passage leading into an old human research complex containing equipment recently activated by alien power sources. They documented the entrance before retreating. A resistance reconnaissance unit subsequently contacted them, offering protection in exchange for their knowledge of the surrounding cave networks.

A former wedding photographer from Dubrovnik, Croatia, this soldier initially struggled to find work after ADVENT introduced government-controlled licensing for independent businesses. They eventually began photographing official ceremonies and administrative events. During one assignment, they captured an image of an ADVENT officer secretly exchanging information with an unknown alien intermediary. Rather than surrender the negatives, they concealed copies inside their photographic equipment and contacted an underground newspaper. Its editors arranged a meeting with a resistance intelligence cell, which later recruited them as a surveillance specialist.

Before the invasion, this soldier worked as a railway dining car attendant in central India, traveling regularly between major regional stations. ADVENT's transport restructuring eliminated most civilian passenger services, but they remained employed in government-operated logistics facilities. While handling discarded catering manifests, they noticed repeated references to a freight carriage that officially did not exist. Their investigation uncovered a clandestine prisoner transport route. They passed the information to a resistance courier and subsequently joined an XCOM-supported underground network responsible for identifying covert ADVENT movements.

This soldier had been a professional glassblower in Murano, Italy, producing decorative pieces for international collectors. During the occupation, ADVENT authorities appropriated several workshops to manufacture components for government installations. They were assigned to produce specialized glass containers but discovered that the specifications were intended for biological containment experiments. Refusing to continue, they damaged the production molds and escaped with several technical drawings. A resistance engineer recognized the significance of their knowledge and arranged their recruitment into an XCOM research support team.

A former commercial truck dispatcher from Nairobi, Kenya, this soldier spent the early occupation coordinating deliveries between agricultural cooperatives and urban markets. Their familiarity with regional transport schedules allowed them to identify unusual military movements disguised as ordinary freight. When a convoy carrying confiscated food supplies was diverted toward a remote ADVENT facility, they deliberately altered its route and redirected the cargo to several isolated settlements. A local resistance commander later approached them, offering a position coordinating supply movements for XCOM operations.

This soldier was a former professional percussionist from Salvador, Brazil, who performed with several independent musical groups before ADVENT restricted public gatherings. They eventually earned a living repairing instruments and teaching private lessons. Their workshop became an informal meeting place for displaced musicians and political dissidents. When an ADVENT surveillance team began investigating the gatherings, they used rehearsals to coordinate the evacuation of several wanted individuals. One of the refugees was a resistance operative who subsequently recommended them for recruitment into an underground communications network.

Before the occupation, this soldier worked as a maritime insurance assessor in Cape Town, South Africa, inspecting damaged vessels and documenting shipping losses. ADVENT retained their services to evaluate seized civilian ships, many of which had been classified as abandoned. While inspecting one vessel, they discovered evidence that its crew had been removed against their will and transported to an alien-controlled installation. They secretly preserved the ship's navigation records and delivered them to a resistance maritime contact. XCOM later recruited them to investigate disappearing civilian transports.

A former occupational therapist from Winnipeg, Canada, this soldier specialized in helping patients recover mobility following industrial accidents. Under ADVENT's healthcare system, rehabilitation services became increasingly limited to government-approved facilities. They began treating injured workers privately, including several resistance sympathizers. When an injured operative revealed that an entire safehouse had been compromised, they helped organize its evacuation and treated the survivors afterward. Their medical expertise and ability to remain calm under pressure eventually earned them a position with an XCOM field medical team.

This soldier had worked as a professional falconer in the deserts of Oman, training birds for wildlife management and traditional hunting demonstrations. ADVENT's expansion into remote areas eventually restricted the use of privately owned animals. They continued working with several trained birds, using them to locate water sources and monitor approaching patrols. When they observed an ADVENT convoy carrying captured villagers, they relayed its location to a nearby resistance cell. The successful interception brought them into contact with XCOM, which recruited them for wilderness reconnaissance.

Formerly a civil aviation safety inspector from Copenhagen, Denmark, this soldier was responsible for investigating mechanical failures and enforcing maintenance standards. ADVENT later reassigned them to inspect government-operated aircraft, where they noticed that several transports had been deliberately stripped of civilian tracking equipment. Their attempts to report the violations were dismissed, and their access credentials were revoked. They subsequently contacted an underground pilot association and supplied evidence of unauthorized military flights. An XCOM aviation officer eventually arranged their recruitment as a technical intelligence specialist.

This soldier grew up in a family of traveling antique dealers in the rural districts of Turkey. Their extensive knowledge of historical artifacts and informal trading networks became useful during the occupation, when ADVENT began confiscating privately held cultural property. They discovered that several valuable objects were being used to conceal encrypted data storage devices. After stealing one such device from an administrative auction, they passed it to a resistance archivist. The archivist recognized their resourcefulness and arranged their introduction to an XCOM intelligence operative.

A former water treatment supervisor from the outskirts of Johannesburg, South Africa, this soldier spent years maintaining municipal filtration systems. ADVENT's occupation brought stricter controls over water distribution, particularly in districts suspected of supporting resistance activity. When their facility received an unexplained chemical shipment, they refused to authorize its use and began conducting independent tests. The results indicated that the substance was intended to make certain neighborhoods temporarily uninhabitable. After leaking the findings, they were forced into hiding and eventually recruited by an XCOM engineering unit.

Before the invasion, this soldier worked as a theatrical costume designer in Madrid, Spain. Their profession survived the early occupation through government-sponsored performances, although most independent productions were eventually prohibited. They secretly maintained a collection of discarded uniforms and identification garments used by people escaping ADVENT-controlled districts. When a resistance courier needed to pass through a heavily monitored checkpoint, they created a convincing disguise that allowed the operative to leave undetected. The courier later arranged their recruitment into an underground infiltration network supporting XCOM.

This soldier had been a professional competitive swimmer from the coastal city of Alexandria, Egypt. After ADVENT closed several independent athletic facilities, they found employment maintaining a public aquatic center. Their familiarity with the city's drainage infrastructure proved useful when a resistance group became trapped inside a flooded underground passage. They guided the survivors through submerged maintenance tunnels and helped them reach the surface. One of the rescued individuals was an XCOM liaison who subsequently recommended them for recruitment into a field operations unit.

A former radio astronomy technician from the Atacama Desert in Chile, this soldier had spent years maintaining remote observation equipment. ADVENT eventually incorporated the facility into a larger communications monitoring network. While servicing an antenna array, they detected a recurring transmission that appeared to originate from somewhere beneath the desert surface. Their attempts to investigate were blocked by government security personnel, prompting them to copy the signal recordings and disappear. A resistance scientific organization later identified the transmission as potentially alien in origin and arranged their transfer to XCOM.

This soldier previously worked as a professional locksmith specializing in historic buildings throughout Edinburgh, Scotland. Their expertise became unexpectedly valuable when ADVENT converted several old government structures into detention centers, retaining their services to maintain original mechanical security systems. During one assignment, they discovered a concealed prisoner compartment behind a sealed archival wall. Rather than report the discovery, they returned after hours and opened the compartment, allowing three detainees to escape. A surviving prisoner later connected them with an XCOM-supported resistance cell.

Before the occupation, this soldier worked as a commercial mushroom cultivator in the forests of eastern Poland. Their underground growing facilities continued operating after ADVENT's agricultural authorities absorbed most surface farms into centralized production systems. They eventually discovered that alien biological material was contaminating several natural fungal colonies. Instead of abandoning their operation, they developed methods to identify and isolate affected crops. A resistance settlement experiencing unexplained food shortages learned of their work and recruited them to manage its underground agricultural supplies.

A former public defender from Buenos Aires, Argentina, this soldier had represented low-income clients before ADVENT dismantled independent judicial institutions. They initially attempted to continue their work through government-appointed legal offices, but their objections to fabricated evidence eventually cost them their position. When an entire group of detainees was scheduled for immediate transfer without hearings, they helped falsify the paperwork needed to delay the convoy. A resistance organizer used the opportunity to extract the prisoners and later offered them a place within the underground movement.

This soldier had worked as a commercial glider pilot in the mountainous regions of Austria. ADVENT's aviation restrictions ended their professional career, but they retained access to an aging aircraft stored at a remote airfield. When a resistance radio operator requested assistance evacuating an injured scout from a mountain settlement, they volunteered despite the risks. The improvised flight succeeded, although their aircraft was subsequently impounded. The rescued scout later arranged their recruitment into an XCOM aviation support network, where their experience with unconventional flight routes proved useful.

Formerly a textile machinery technician in Dhaka, Bangladesh, this soldier worked in a large garment factory before ADVENT reorganized the city's industrial sector. Their responsibilities involved maintaining older looms and repairing automated production equipment. After discovering that several machines had been modified to manufacture components for ADVENT combat armor, they began introducing subtle defects into selected production runs. The resulting equipment failures disrupted a regional supply shipment. A resistance operative investigating the incident eventually traced the sabotage to their workshop and recruited them.

This soldier had been a professional mountain botanist working in the highlands of Ecuador, cataloguing rare plant species for an independent research institution. ADVENT later restricted access to several protected regions, citing unexplained environmental hazards. During an unauthorized expedition, they discovered that an alien installation was altering the local vegetation through an unknown biological process. They collected samples and narrowly escaped a patrol sent to secure the area. Their findings reached an underground scientific collective, which arranged for XCOM to recruit them as a field research specialist.

A former prison librarian from Buenos Aires, this soldier spent the occupation maintaining reading rooms in several government detention facilities. Their position gave them access to correspondence and confiscated personal documents that were otherwise destroyed after processing. They began secretly preserving letters from prisoners whose identities had been erased from official records. When a resistance contact requested evidence of an unauthorized detention program, they supplied an extensive collection of documents. The information helped expose the facility, and the contact subsequently arranged their recruitment into XCOM's intelligence network.

This soldier worked as an independent bicycle frame builder in Copenhagen, Denmark, before the invasion. ADVENT's transportation policies gradually eliminated private manufacturing, but they continued producing durable bicycles from salvaged components for residents of isolated settlements. When a resistance cell lost access to its regular supply route, they began transporting medical equipment using specially modified cargo bicycles. An ADVENT patrol eventually intercepted one of their deliveries, forcing them to abandon their workshop. The resistance group later recommended them to XCOM for logistics and field maintenance duties.

Before joining the resistance, this soldier worked as a professional insect researcher in the rainforests of Madagascar. Their studies originally focused on biological pest control and the preservation of endangered species. During the occupation, ADVENT offered funding for research into newly introduced alien organisms, but the proposed experiments involved releasing modified specimens into protected ecosystems. They refused to participate and removed several research samples before the laboratory was closed. A resistance scientific team later recruited them to investigate alien insect biology and environmental contamination.

This soldier had been a commercial locksmith and safe technician in Buenos Aires, Argentina, specializing in obsolete banking equipment. ADVENT's centralized financial system made much of their previous work unnecessary, so they began repairing mechanical safes for private collectors. One assignment brought them to an abandoned municipal building where they discovered a hidden compartment containing pre-invasion resistance records. After decoding the documents, they contacted the original network's surviving members. An XCOM liaison subsequently recruited them for their mechanical expertise and knowledge of concealed storage systems.

A former professional ice road driver from northern Canada, this soldier had spent winters transporting heavy equipment across frozen lakes and remote settlements. ADVENT's expansion into the region disrupted traditional freight routes, leaving several communities dependent on unreliable government deliveries. When an ADVENT transport vehicle became stranded during a severe blizzard, they discovered that its cargo included confiscated medical supplies intended for a nearby settlement. They diverted the shipment and helped deliver it to the community. A resistance quartermaster later recruited them for wilderness logistics operations.

This soldier had been a ceramic engineer in Izmir, Turkey, working on heat-resistant industrial materials before ADVENT took control of the manufacturing sector. Their expertise was retained for the production of specialized components used in government infrastructure. During a routine materials inspection, they discovered that several ceramic compounds were being incorporated into alien containment chambers. After learning that the chambers were intended for human experimentation, they copied the technical specifications and fled. A resistance engineer later arranged their recruitment into an XCOM research and development team.

Formerly a professional wedding planner in Nairobi, Kenya, this soldier spent the early occupation organizing private ceremonies under increasingly restrictive public gathering regulations. Their work required maintaining extensive contact lists and coordinating transportation, catering, and venue access. These connections eventually allowed them to arrange discreet meetings between resistance sympathizers who otherwise had no means of communicating. When one gathering was exposed, they helped several attendees escape through a neighboring construction site. A resistance coordinator later offered them a position managing clandestine meetings and personnel movements.

This soldier had worked as a deep-sea salvage diver off the coast of Portugal, recovering equipment from sunken vessels and abandoned offshore installations. ADVENT later contracted them to inspect a submerged communications platform that had stopped transmitting. Beneath the structure, they discovered an alien device attached to the ocean floor, surrounded by unusual biological growth. They documented the site before a government recovery team arrived. After sharing the information with an underground scientific group, they were recruited by XCOM to assist with investigations involving submerged alien technology.

A former professional puppeteer and ventriloquist from Prague, Czech Republic, this soldier had performed for children's hospitals and community theaters before the occupation. When ADVENT restricted independent performances, they began traveling between settlements as an informal entertainer. Their unusual performances provided cover for passing coded messages between resistance contacts, with different puppet arrangements representing specific instructions. After an ADVENT informant began monitoring their movements, a resistance courier arranged their relocation. They were eventually recruited into an XCOM intelligence network specializing in unconventional communications.

This soldier had been a railway bridge inspector in northern Spain, responsible for identifying structural weaknesses in aging transport infrastructure. ADVENT's military logistics expansion brought increased traffic to several neglected bridges, many of which were dangerously overloaded. When they discovered that a damaged crossing was scheduled to carry a heavily armed convoy, they deliberately exaggerated its structural condition to force a temporary closure. The delay allowed a nearby resistance cell to evacuate an exposed settlement. An XCOM engineer subsequently recruited them for infrastructure assessment and sabotage planning.

Before the invasion, this soldier operated a small independent bookstore in the city of Ghent, Belgium. ADVENT's cultural authorities gradually removed unapproved publications, leaving their shelves increasingly empty. They began maintaining a private archive of banned literature, historical records, and underground newspapers beneath the shop. When government inspectors discovered the collection, they escaped through a neighboring building and carried several irreplaceable documents with them. A resistance historian later offered them protection and introduced them to XCOM, where their archival knowledge became valuable for intelligence research.

This soldier worked as a professional veterinary anesthetist in the rural districts of Argentina, specializing in the treatment of large animals. ADVENT's agricultural consolidation program introduced unfamiliar livestock breeds requiring specialized medical attention. During one procedure, they discovered an implanted alien monitoring device beneath an animal's skin. Further investigation revealed that the animals were being used to test a biological tracking system. They removed several devices and secretly supplied them to a resistance researcher, who subsequently arranged their recruitment into an XCOM medical research unit.

A former industrial diver from the port city of Odessa, Ukraine, this soldier specialized in repairing submerged pipelines and underwater electrical equipment. ADVENT retained their services for several years, assigning them to restricted harbor installations. During one inspection, they found evidence that an abandoned civilian submarine had been converted into an unauthorized prisoner transport. They disabled its navigation equipment before the next departure and transmitted its location to an underground contact. A resistance maritime commander later recruited them to support operations involving coastal infrastructure.

This soldier had worked as a professional auctioneer in Vienna, Austria, before ADVENT occupation authorities nationalized most major auction houses. They were retained to catalogue confiscated private collections, which frequently included property seized from political dissidents. While examining a collection of antique musical instruments, they discovered a concealed data storage device containing records of illegal government transactions. They copied the information and arranged its transfer to an underground journalist. The journalist subsequently introduced them to a resistance intelligence officer, who recruited them as an asset identification specialist.

Before the invasion, this soldier worked as a rural telecommunications installer in the Scottish Highlands. Their responsibilities included maintaining old telephone lines and restoring connections between isolated communities. ADVENT eventually replaced much of the network with monitored digital infrastructure, but many remote settlements continued relying on the older equipment. When a resistance group lost contact with several outposts, they restored a forgotten telephone exchange and established an independent communications route. An XCOM signals officer later contacted them and arranged their recruitment as a communications technician.

A former professional glass diver from the coastal communities of Greece, this soldier specialized in collecting marine specimens and recovering lost equipment from shallow waters. During the occupation, they discovered unusual deposits surrounding several restricted offshore structures. ADVENT authorities repeatedly denied the existence of the installations, but the soldier continued documenting the changes to the seabed. When a patrol seized their research equipment, they escaped with a set of handwritten observations. A resistance scientific team later recruited them to investigate alien activity beneath coastal waters.

This soldier had been a municipal building inspector in Tallinn, Estonia, before ADVENT reorganized local government. Their occupation required regular access to residential buildings, construction sites, and public infrastructure. While examining a newly renovated apartment block, they discovered that several floors had been constructed around concealed observation rooms equipped with alien surveillance technology. They quietly warned the residents and helped them relocate before the building was sealed. A resistance intelligence officer later recruited them to identify other compromised structures throughout the city.

Formerly a professional horologist in Geneva, Switzerland, this soldier specialized in repairing precision instruments and antique chronometers. Their work continued during the occupation, largely through private commissions from government officials and wealthy collaborators. One customer brought them a damaged wristwatch containing a miniature electronic component that did not match any known human design. Rather than return it, they investigated the mechanism and discovered a hidden tracking device. After passing their findings to a resistance technician, they were recruited to help analyze alien surveillance equipment.

This soldier had worked as a commercial salt miner in the deserts of western China before ADVENT expanded its industrial operations into the region. Their knowledge of underground excavation techniques remained useful after conventional mining was replaced by automated systems. When an underground settlement experienced unexplained tremors, they volunteered to investigate its abandoned tunnels. They discovered an ADVENT drilling operation approaching the settlement from below and helped residents evacuate through an older mining shaft. A resistance commander later recruited them for subterranean reconnaissance.

A former professional voice coach from Cape Town, South Africa, this soldier had trained actors and broadcasters before ADVENT imposed restrictions on independent media. Their expertise in vocal imitation eventually became useful to an underground group attempting to bypass voice-controlled security systems. When an operative was captured during an infiltration attempt, they impersonated an ADVENT administrator over a communications channel, delaying the security response long enough for the rescue team to arrive. The operation attracted the attention of an XCOM intelligence officer, who offered them a place in the resistance.

Before the invasion, this soldier was a commercial orchard manager in the rural districts of northern Japan. ADVENT's agricultural restructuring initially preserved their employment, but their orchard was eventually selected for conversion into an automated production facility. Rather than surrender the land, they organized neighboring farmers to conceal traditional seed stock and preserve independent cultivation methods. When government inspectors arrived, the group dispersed into nearby woodland. A resistance settlement later discovered their agricultural network and recruited them to help maintain food supplies for displaced civilians.

This soldier had worked as a professional demolition surveyor in the industrial districts of Manchester, England. Their responsibilities included assessing unsafe buildings before scheduled redevelopment projects. During the occupation, they noticed that ADVENT was demolishing selected structures despite their sound condition, often leaving unexplained underground cavities. Their investigation uncovered a concealed network of alien communication conduits. After secretly mapping the tunnels, they passed the information to a resistance engineer. XCOM subsequently recruited them to assist with identifying structural weaknesses in alien installations.

A former professional pastry chef from Montreal, Canada, this soldier had managed the kitchen of a respected hotel before ADVENT took control of the city's hospitality industry. Their employment continued under a government-appointed manager, although food shortages increasingly affected civilian staff. They began using the hotel's delivery schedule to conceal medicine and small equipment shipments for local dissidents. When an ADVENT inspection discovered the hidden supplies, they escaped through the building's commercial laundry system. A resistance quartermaster later recruited them for their organizational skills and established supply contacts.

This soldier had been a professional meteorological balloon technician in the rural districts of Kazakhstan, maintaining high-altitude weather monitoring equipment. ADVENT retained their services after the invasion, but the installation eventually began receiving unexplained transmissions from unidentified aerial objects. When they discovered that the equipment was being used to track resistance aircraft rather than monitor weather conditions, they deliberately altered its readings and concealed the original data. A resistance pilot later identified the interference and arranged their recruitment into an XCOM technical support team.

A former occupational safety inspector from Brno, Czech Republic, this soldier spent the early occupation examining industrial workplaces for compliance with ADVENT regulations. Their reports were routinely altered by supervisors seeking to conceal dangerous production conditions. After a factory accident left several workers permanently injured, they refused to falsify the investigation and secretly preserved the original inspection records. A worker involved in the incident later introduced them to a resistance organizer, who recruited them to investigate industrial facilities supporting ADVENT military operations.

Before the invasion, this soldier worked as a professional pearl diver in the coastal communities of Bahrain. ADVENT's maritime restrictions gradually eliminated independent diving operations, forcing them to accept occasional maintenance contracts at government-controlled offshore installations. During one assignment, they discovered a submerged transport container containing personal belongings from several missing civilians. They recovered a data recorder before the installation's security systems activated. A resistance contact helped them escape the area and subsequently arranged their recruitment into an XCOM-supported maritime reconnaissance team.

A former prison transport driver from Lyon, France, this soldier had worked for a private security contractor before ADVENT absorbed the company's operations. Their assignments eventually involved transferring detainees between administrative facilities. After recognizing that several prisoners were being transported under false identities, they began altering delivery schedules to create opportunities for escape. One successful diversion allowed a resistance organizer to disappear before reaching an ADVENT detention center. The organizer later contacted them through an underground network and arranged their recruitment into XCOM.

This soldier had been a professional glass conservator in Stockholm, Sweden, restoring stained-glass windows and historical architectural decorations. ADVENT's occupation initially had little effect on their work, but government authorities eventually ordered the removal of religious and historical imagery from public buildings. They secretly preserved several confiscated window panels in a disused warehouse. When an ADVENT inspection team discovered the collection, they escaped with assistance from a group of preservationists who maintained underground resistance contacts. Their knowledge of historic buildings later proved valuable to XCOM infiltration teams.

Formerly a commercial horse breeder in the rural districts of Mongolia, this soldier spent years maintaining a small herd adapted to harsh weather and difficult terrain. ADVENT's expansion into the region introduced automated agricultural facilities, displacing many independent breeders. They refused government compensation and continued trading animals with isolated communities. When an ADVENT patrol attempted to confiscate their herd, they led the animals through an abandoned border trail, helping several refugees escape at the same time. A resistance scout later recruited them for wilderness operations.

A former broadcast engineer from Lagos, Nigeria, this soldier maintained television transmission equipment for several regional stations before the occupation. They secretly modified the equipment to create brief gaps in the interference pattern, allowing resistance radio operators to communicate. An underground communications coordinator identified the source and offered them a position supporting XCOM's signal operations.

This soldier had worked as a professional horseracing handicapper in Buenos Aires, Argentina, analyzing performance records and advising betting syndicates. After sharing the findings with a resistance intelligence group, they were recruited to assist with predicting patrol movements and identifying suspicious administrative activity.

Before the invasion, this soldier operated a small independent ceramics workshop in the rural districts of Portugal. Their experiments revealed that the material contained alien compounds that affected nearby electronic devices. They passed samples to an underground researcher, who arranged their introduction to XCOM's engineering division.

A former professional ice hockey referee from Winnipeg, Canada, this soldier had spent years officiating regional leagues before ADVENT prohibited independent sporting competitions. Rather than assist the security personnel, they opened an emergency exit and allowed the crowd to disperse. A resistance operative who witnessed the incident later recruited them for crowd control and field security duties.

This soldier had been a professional landscape architect in Cape Town, South Africa, designing public parks and urban green spaces. When an ADVENT security inspection uncovered the modifications, they abandoned their position and disappeared into the surrounding districts. A resistance cell subsequently recruited them to assist with urban concealment and infiltration planning.

Formerly a commercial refrigeration inspector in Buenos Aires, Argentina, this soldier specialized in evaluating cold-storage facilities and food distribution warehouses. They preserved the facility's maintenance logs and distributed copies through an underground technical network. An XCOM scientist later requested their assistance in identifying weaknesses in alien containment systems.

This soldier had worked as a professional puppeteer in the rural communities of southern India, traveling between villages to perform traditional stories.
