Their familiarity with local folklore helped them recognize that government officials were deliberately replacing traditional historical accounts with fabricated occupation narratives. They began distributing handwritten versions of the original stories, eventually attracting the attention of an underground cultural resistance group that introduced them to XCOM.

A former airport baggage systems technician from Frankfurt, Germany, this soldier maintained automated sorting equipment before ADVENT consolidated civilian air travel. They were retained to service a government logistics terminal, where they discovered that certain containers were being diverted through a separate scanning network. After investigating, they found evidence of undeclared shipments containing confiscated civilian technology. They copied the terminal's routing records and transmitted them to a resistance contact. The information helped identify an ADVENT supply depot, and they were subsequently recruited by XCOM.

Before the invasion, this soldier was a professional falconry equipment maker in the rural districts of Kazakhstan. Their workshop produced specialized leather gloves, protective hoods, and training equipment for local bird handlers. ADVENT's restrictions on privately owned animals eventually reduced their business, but they continued repairing equipment for remote communities. When a resistance settlement requested assistance transporting small communication devices across open terrain, they developed lightweight carrying harnesses for trained birds. A resistance quartermaster recognized their ingenuity and recommended them for recruitment.

This soldier had been a municipal traffic signal engineer in Mexico City, responsible for maintaining the city's aging road infrastructure. ADVENT replaced much of the existing traffic system with centralized automated control, but several older districts retained independent signal networks. After noticing that ADVENT patrols were consistently avoiding certain intersections, they investigated and discovered a concealed surveillance grid. They secretly modified the traffic controllers to disrupt the system during scheduled patrol movements. A resistance operative eventually traced the interference to their workshop and recruited them.

A former professional glass artist from Reykjavík, Iceland, this soldier specialized in creating optical lenses for scientific instruments. Their work initially attracted interest from ADVENT researchers, who contracted them to manufacture components for an unidentified imaging system. They eventually realized that the specifications were intended for equipment capable of detecting human biological signatures through walls. Unwilling to contribute to mass surveillance, they sabotaged the final production batch and fled with several technical drawings. A resistance scientist later arranged their recruitment into an XCOM research support team.

This soldier worked as a commercial beekeeper in the mountainous regions of Georgia, maintaining colonies that supplied honey and pollination services to local farms. ADVENT's introduction of synthetic agricultural systems reduced demand for traditional beekeeping, but they continued operating several remote apiaries. When an unexplained chemical treatment began killing entire colonies, they traced the contamination to an ADVENT supply facility. Their investigation attracted government attention, forcing them to abandon their operation. A resistance agricultural specialist later recruited them to help identify alien contaminants affecting local ecosystems.

Before the occupation, this soldier worked as a professional sports physiotherapist in Johannesburg, South Africa. Their clients included several prominent athletes who were later recruited into ADVENT-sponsored sporting programs. When one athlete suffered a severe injury during a government exhibition, they discovered that medical staff had concealed evidence of experimental performance-enhancing implants. They refused to sign the official treatment report and began documenting similar cases. A former patient eventually connected them with a resistance medical network, which recruited them to provide rehabilitation services for injured operatives.

A former underground utility mapper from Helsinki, Finland, this soldier specialized in documenting forgotten drainage channels, electrical conduits, and maintenance tunnels. ADVENT's urban reconstruction projects frequently relied on outdated municipal records, allowing them to retain temporary employment despite their independent background. When a resistance group became trapped beneath a government checkpoint, they provided an alternate route through a sealed utility corridor. The successful evacuation brought them to the attention of an XCOM reconnaissance officer, who recruited them to map concealed access routes around occupied settlements.

This soldier had worked as a professional taxidermist in rural Scotland, preserving wildlife specimens for museums and private collectors. During the occupation, they received an unusual commission from an ADVENT research assistant who requested the preservation of several unidentified animal remains. They recognized that the specimens had been altered through surgical procedures inconsistent with ordinary veterinary practice. After secretly photographing the remains, they passed the evidence to an underground scientific group. Their detailed knowledge of anatomy eventually earned them a position with XCOM's research support personnel.

Formerly a commercial diving instructor in the Philippines, this soldier taught recreational diving and underwater safety around the islands of Palawan. ADVENT's maritime security restrictions eventually ended their business, but they continued guiding local fishermen through dangerous coastal waters. When an alien patrol vessel became stranded near a reef, they observed several human prisoners escaping into the water. They helped the survivors reach a concealed fishing settlement and contacted a resistance organization. Their underwater navigation skills later made them a valuable addition to XCOM's reconnaissance operations.

This soldier had been a professional bookbinder in Edinburgh, Scotland, restoring rare manuscripts and producing archival documents. ADVENT's cultural authorities initially allowed their business to continue, provided that all publications were registered. They secretly used discarded binding materials to conceal microfilm records and handwritten resistance messages inside ordinary books. When an underground archive was discovered, they helped preserve its contents by distributing the documents among several unsuspecting customers. One of the archive's surviving custodians later arranged their recruitment into XCOM's intelligence network.

A former industrial crane operator from Gdańsk, Poland, this soldier spent years working in commercial shipyards before ADVENT took control of the port facilities. Their experience with heavy machinery earned them a position at a government logistics terminal. During an overnight shift, they noticed that an incoming container had been improperly secured and contained several living human captives. They delayed the unloading process and used the crane to place the container beyond the reach of security personnel. A resistance operative subsequently helped the prisoners escape and recruited them for logistical operations.

Before the invasion, this soldier was a professional sound engineer in Buenos Aires, Argentina, working with theaters, recording studios, and live music venues. ADVENT's restrictions on independent broadcasting eventually pushed them into maintaining public announcement systems. While servicing a government building, they discovered that its speakers were transmitting high-frequency signals alongside ordinary propaganda broadcasts. They modified the system to interfere with the signal and began documenting its effects on nearby civilians. A resistance scientist investigating the transmissions later recruited them to assist with electronic warfare research.

This soldier had worked as a rural veterinarian in the mountains of northern Pakistan, treating livestock belonging to isolated farming communities. ADVENT's agricultural expansion introduced unfamiliar animal diseases, and local authorities repeatedly denied requests for medical assistance. After discovering that several affected herds had been deliberately exposed to experimental pathogens, they began collecting samples and treating animals without government authorization. A resistance settlement eventually contacted them after experiencing similar outbreaks. Their veterinary expertise and familiarity with remote communities secured them a position within an XCOM medical support network.

A former professional salvage auctioneer from Hamburg, Germany, this soldier specialized in evaluating machinery recovered from abandoned factories and shipyards. ADVENT's industrial restructuring created a steady supply of confiscated equipment, and they initially worked for government contractors. They eventually discovered that several supposedly worthless machines contained hidden alien components that were being removed before public auctions. Rather than report the theft, they began recording the serial numbers and identifying the buyers. A resistance intelligence group later recruited them to trace the movement of alien technology through civilian markets.

This soldier had been a professional mountaineering equipment designer in Innsbruck, Austria, specializing in lightweight climbing systems and emergency safety devices. ADVENT's restrictions on independent expeditions ended most of their commercial work, but they continued developing equipment for small wilderness communities. When a resistance patrol became stranded on a steep mountain ridge during an ADVENT pursuit, they delivered an improvised climbing system that allowed the group to escape. Impressed by their practical engineering skills, the patrol commander recommended them for recruitment into XCOM.

Before the invasion, this soldier worked as a professional radio drama producer in Lagos, Nigeria. Their studio was eventually absorbed into ADVENT's government broadcasting network, where they were assigned to produce scripted public information programs. They began embedding subtle inconsistencies in the broadcasts to alert listeners when security operations were underway. When an ADVENT editor discovered the alterations, they fled the studio with a collection of original transmission recordings. A resistance communications officer later recruited them to assist with psychological operations and clandestine broadcasts.

A former commercial mushroom inspector from the Netherlands, this soldier specialized in detecting contamination and maintaining agricultural quality standards. ADVENT's introduction of genetically modified crops initially increased demand for their expertise, but they became concerned when government farms began concealing unusual growth patterns. After discovering that an entire production facility was cultivating fungal organisms derived from alien biological material, they secretly removed several samples. Their findings reached an underground agricultural research collective, which arranged their recruitment into an XCOM scientific support unit.

This soldier had been a professional competitive archer from Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, training in traditional and modern target disciplines. ADVENT's restrictions on independent sporting events ended their competitive career, and they eventually found work maintaining equipment at a government recreation facility. During an unauthorized hunting expedition outside the city, they witnessed an ADVENT patrol attempting to capture a group of escaped detainees. They intervened using their bow and guided the survivors into the surrounding hills. A resistance scout later recruited them for their accuracy and wilderness experience.

Formerly a medical equipment technician in Manila, Philippines, this soldier specialized in repairing diagnostic machines and surgical instruments. During the occupation, they worked at an ADVENT-approved hospital, where they noticed that several medical devices were being modified to record patient neurological activity without consent. After discovering that the data was being transmitted to an alien research facility, they copied the transmission logs and disabled the equipment. An underground physician helped them escape before their activities were discovered and later arranged their recruitment by XCOM.

This soldier had been a professional saltwater aquaculture technician in the coastal regions of Vietnam. Their work involved maintaining fish farms and monitoring water quality in large commercial ponds. ADVENT eventually introduced an unfamiliar aquatic organism into several government-controlled facilities, claiming it would improve food production. They discovered that the organism was consuming native fish populations and producing toxic waste. After leaking the findings, they were forced to abandon their position. A resistance settlement recruited them to help restore damaged freshwater and coastal food supplies.

A former theatrical fight choreographer from London, England, this soldier specialized in designing realistic stage combat for film and television productions. After ADVENT restricted independent entertainment, they found work coordinating demonstrations for government recruitment campaigns. During one performance, an ADVENT officer ordered them to stage a fabricated incident depicting resistance fighters attacking civilians. They refused and instead helped several performers escape the controlled venue. One of the actors later introduced them to a resistance cell, which recruited them to train inexperienced volunteers in close-quarters techniques.

Before the invasion, this soldier worked as a professional railway locomotive restorer in the industrial districts of Łódź, Poland. ADVENT's automated transport system made their specialist skills increasingly unnecessary, but they continued restoring obsolete engines for private collectors. When a resistance settlement needed a way to move supplies through a disused rail corridor, they volunteered to restore an old maintenance locomotive. The improvised transport system remained operational for several months before ADVENT discovered the route. A resistance logistics officer later recommended them to XCOM.

This soldier had worked as a commercial pest controller in the suburbs of Brisbane, Australia, specializing in the removal of dangerous insects and invasive species. During the occupation, ADVENT contracted them to investigate unusual infestations near a restricted industrial complex. They discovered that the insects were being attracted to an alien waste disposal site and had developed abnormal resistance to conventional pesticides. When their report was suppressed, they retained the samples and contacted an underground research group. XCOM later recruited them for their knowledge of biological hazards.

A former customs documentation officer from Tangier, Morocco, this soldier had processed shipping manifests and import declarations at the city's commercial port. ADVENT's takeover transformed the port into a heavily monitored military supply center, but their position remained unchanged. They gradually discovered that several containers were being transferred without customs records, often arriving from facilities that did not officially exist. They began copying the shipping data and passing it to a resistance courier. After an ADVENT audit exposed their activities, they escaped and joined an XCOM-supported intelligence network.

This soldier had been a professional landscape painter in the rural districts of Ireland, specializing in detailed studies of abandoned estates and coastal settlements. ADVENT's occupation initially left their livelihood largely untouched, although government authorities increasingly discouraged independent exhibitions. While painting near a restricted military installation, they noticed that patrol movements followed a repeating pattern visible from the surrounding hills. They recorded the observations in a series of landscape sketches and passed them to a resistance scout. Their unusual intelligence-gathering method eventually earned them a place in an XCOM reconnaissance unit.

Formerly a professional optician in Rotterdam, Netherlands, this soldier operated a small business specializing in custom lenses and corrective eyewear. ADVENT's medical system eventually absorbed independent optical services, but they continued repairing older equipment for residents unable to obtain government-issued replacements. One customer brought them a damaged pair of experimental glasses containing a concealed alien sensor. After examining the device, they discovered it could detect certain forms of biological camouflage. A resistance scientist subsequently recruited them to help investigate Faceless detection technology.

Before the invasion, this soldier worked as a commercial irrigation designer in the agricultural districts of northern Mexico. When a government facility diverted an entire river branch away from a settlement, they secretly modified the control system to restore part of the original flow. The affected community survived the resulting shortages and introduced them to a resistance organizer, who later recruited them for infrastructure operations.

This soldier had been a professional maritime signalman in the coastal regions of Scotland, working aboard commercial vessels and harbor service boats. ADVENT's occupation restricted civilian shipping, but they continued operating within government-controlled maritime networks. During one voyage, they intercepted a distress transmission from a vessel officially recorded as having been decommissioned months earlier. They altered the ship's reported position and helped a resistance crew reach the survivors before ADVENT patrols arrived. Their communications expertise subsequently brought them into an XCOM naval support network.

A former professional watch repairer from Bucharest, Romania, this soldier specialized in restoring mechanical timepieces and precision instruments. When a resistance operative arrived with a damaged timing mechanism used in an explosive device, they repaired it without asking its purpose. The operative later returned with a recruitment offer, recognizing their ability to work accurately with delicate equipment under difficult conditions.

This soldier had been a commercial wildlife ranger in the savannah regions of Kenya, monitoring animal populations and preventing illegal hunting. ADVENT's expansion introduced new restrictions on protected land, and several former conservation areas became inaccessible government zones. While tracking a missing elephant herd, they discovered that an alien patrol was using the animals' migration routes to conceal its movements. They documented the patrol and transmitted its location to a nearby resistance cell. Their wilderness expertise eventually earned them a place with XCOM's reconnaissance personnel.

Before the occupation, this soldier worked as a professional industrial electrician in the suburbs of Osaka, Japan. After discovering that several electrical systems had been modified to deliver lethal surges to workers attempting to disable production equipment, they began secretly installing emergency bypasses. When an industrial accident exposed their alterations, they fled with the help of several factory workers. A resistance engineer later recruited them for sabotage and infrastructure maintenance.

This soldier had been a professional documentary sound recordist in the Amazon region of Brazil, specializing in capturing wildlife and environmental recordings. Their recordings eventually revealed unusual sounds associated with underground alien excavation equipment. When government officials ordered the destruction of their original files, they concealed copies on several portable devices and distributed them through independent research contacts. A resistance scientist later recruited them to assist with acoustic surveillance and alien activity detection.

A former professional tailor from Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, this soldier specialized in repairing military surplus clothing and producing custom protective garments. A local resistance quartermaster eventually offered them a permanent position supporting XCOM operations.

This soldier had worked as a professional lighthouse electrician on the coast of Brittany, France. A resistance maritime organization later recruited them to maintain communications equipment for XCOM-supported operations.

Before the invasion, this soldier was a professional meteorite collector and amateur astronomer in the rural districts of Argentina. While tracking a meteor shower, they detected several unidentified objects moving in formation above the atmosphere. Their subsequent observations revealed a recurring pattern associated with ADVENT aerial deployments. After sharing the data through an underground astronomy forum, they were contacted by a resistance researcher and eventually recruited to assist with tracking alien spacecraft.

This soldier had been a professional funeral director in Glasgow, Scotland, managing a family business before ADVENT's occupation. After preserving copies of the original records, they passed the information to an underground legal organization. One of its members later introduced them to XCOM, where their familiarity with government procedures and medical documentation proved useful.

A former professional textile dyer from Lahore, Pakistan, this soldier specialized in producing durable natural pigments for traditional fabrics. They eventually developed a pigment that remained visible under certain alien optical sensors, making it useful for marking hidden paths and supply caches. ADVENT initially retained them to analyze population health data, but they gradually noticed that entire districts were being excluded from official medical reports. Their investigation revealed a correlation between unexplained disappearances and visits from specialized ADVENT medical units. They leaked the findings to an underground journalist, who connected them with an XCOM intelligence officer seeking expertise in epidemiological analysis.

This soldier had been a professional commercial diver working on underwater archaeological projects near Malta. ADVENT's maritime restrictions eventually forced them to abandon independent exploration and accept government maintenance contracts. During an inspection of a submerged cable network, they discovered that several sections had been deliberately severed and replaced with unfamiliar alien components. They photographed the installation before a security team arrived. Their evidence reached a resistance scientific group, which recruited them to assist with underwater investigations and the recovery of submerged alien technology.

A former professional furniture upholsterer from Buenos Aires, Argentina, this soldier specialized in restoring antique seating and producing custom interiors for commercial buildings. During the occupation, they began receiving commissions from government offices and wealthy collaborators. One assignment revealed a concealed compartment inside an executive chair containing confiscated personal identification documents. They discovered that the records belonged to civilians who had disappeared from official databases. Rather than return the documents, they delivered them to an underground legal organization and were later recruited by XCOM as an intelligence archivist.

This soldier had worked as a professional cave rescue medic in the mountainous regions of northern Spain. Their experience involved treating injuries in confined spaces and coordinating difficult underground evacuations. After ADVENT established a restricted research site near a known cave system, several local explorers disappeared while investigating unusual activity. They organized a volunteer search and discovered an injured survivor near a sealed underground entrance. The survivor was a resistance operative carrying valuable intelligence. After assisting with the extraction, they were offered a place in an XCOM field medical unit.

Formerly a professional commercial beekeeper in the rural districts of Bulgaria, this soldier specialized in maintaining colonies adapted to cold mountain conditions. ADVENT's agricultural authorities attempted to replace traditional pollination systems with automated equipment, but independent farmers continued seeking their services. When an alien transport crash contaminated several nearby apiaries, they developed a method for identifying affected colonies before the contamination spread. A resistance settlement later requested their assistance in restoring local agriculture, and their subsequent work earned them recruitment into XCOM's environmental research network.

A former professional civil surveyor from Montevideo, Uruguay, this soldier specialized in measuring property boundaries and mapping urban development projects. ADVENT's occupation brought widespread changes to official land records, and they were assigned to verify several government relocation zones. Their measurements revealed that a proposed residential redevelopment concealed a large underground structure extending far beyond the official construction plans. They secretly copied the survey data and passed it to an underground journalist. An XCOM intelligence officer later recruited them to identify concealed alien installations.

This soldier had worked as a professional accordion repairer in the rural districts of Romania, maintaining instruments for local musicians and traveling performers. ADVENT's restrictions on independent gatherings reduced their business, but they continued repairing instruments through private contacts. One customer brought them an accordion containing a miniature radio transmitter concealed inside its bellows. They repaired the device and discovered that it was being used to coordinate messages between resistance cells. The original owner subsequently introduced them to an underground communications group, which recruited them to maintain clandestine equipment.

Before the invasion, this soldier worked as a commercial aircraft upholstery technician in Toulouse, France. Their expertise involved repairing seating systems and cabin interiors for civilian passenger aircraft. ADVENT's occupation eventually transferred the facility to military production, where they discovered that several aircraft were being modified with concealed restraint systems intended for human transport. They refused to complete the work and sabotaged the specialized fittings before escaping. A resistance aviation specialist later recruited them to inspect captured transports and identify concealed prisoner compartments.

This soldier had been a professional orchard grafting specialist in the rural districts of northern Spain. Their occupation involved preserving traditional fruit varieties and helping small farmers maintain productive trees. ADVENT's agricultural authorities began replacing local crops with genetically standardized alternatives, threatening the region's traditional farming communities. They secretly preserved rare seed stock and taught several families how to maintain independent orchards. When government inspectors discovered the operation, they escaped into the surrounding hills. A resistance settlement later recruited them to establish sustainable food production.

A former professional customs dog handler from Hamburg, Germany, this soldier trained animals to detect prohibited materials and contraband shipments. ADVENT initially retained their expertise for inspecting cargo entering government-controlled warehouses. They eventually noticed that trained animals became unusually agitated near certain sealed containers, despite official claims that the contents were harmless. After investigating, they discovered evidence of alien biological material. They refused to continue inspections and secretly contacted a resistance researcher, who recruited them to help develop methods for detecting concealed alien substances.

This soldier had worked as a professional stage carpenter in Wellington, New Zealand, constructing scenery and mechanical effects for theatrical productions. ADVENT's occupation eliminated most independent theaters, but they found temporary employment building sets for government ceremonies. During one assignment, they discovered that a stage structure concealed a temporary holding area used to detain protestors before public events. They modified the stage mechanisms to create an escape opportunity during a ceremony. A rescued dissident later arranged their recruitment into a resistance engineering team.

Formerly a professional glacier monitoring technician in the Andes of Argentina, this soldier specialized in measuring ice movement and predicting dangerous glacial collapses. ADVENT's expansion into remote mountain regions brought several restricted scientific installations near their observation sites. Their instruments began registering unexplained seismic activity beneath one facility, followed by sudden changes in local ice movement. Suspecting underground excavation, they transmitted their findings to an independent research group. A resistance scientist later recruited them to monitor alien construction activity in mountainous terrain.

This soldier had been a professional furniture maker in the industrial districts of Osaka, Japan. Their workshop specialized in producing durable wooden equipment for schools, hospitals, and public buildings. ADVENT's industrial consolidation eventually forced them into government manufacturing, where they discovered that several production lines were using confiscated human property as raw materials. They refused to continue and began producing hidden compartments in ordinary furniture to help dissidents conceal documents and supplies. A resistance quartermaster later recruited them for equipment construction and safehouse preparation.

A former professional livestock auctioneer from the rural districts of Ireland, this soldier specialized in evaluating cattle and coordinating sales between independent farmers. ADVENT's agricultural policies gradually eliminated private livestock markets, but they continued operating unofficial auctions. When a government representative attempted to seize several healthy herds under false disease regulations, they organized the farmers to move the animals before the confiscation teams arrived. The resulting operation attracted the attention of a resistance supply coordinator, who recruited them to manage livestock and food distribution among remote settlements.

This soldier worked as a professional underwater pipeline welder in the coastal regions of Norway. Their expertise was retained by ADVENT's energy administration, which assigned them to repair damaged infrastructure near a restricted offshore installation. During one operation, they discovered a section of pipeline containing an unfamiliar biological substance that appeared to be growing through the metal. They collected a sample and warned their crew to evacuate. A resistance scientific team later recruited them to help investigate alien contamination of industrial systems.

Before the invasion, this soldier worked as a professional court translator in Montreal, Canada, specializing in several European and Asian languages. ADVENT's occupation eventually dismantled independent legal institutions, but they were retained to translate administrative documents for government officials. Their access to confidential records revealed that several detainees were being transferred under fabricated identities. They began quietly correcting the records and alerting relatives through underground channels. When their activities were discovered, a resistance group helped them escape and arranged their recruitment into XCOM's intelligence division.

This soldier had been a professional fishing net manufacturer in the coastal districts of Senegal. Their small business supplied local fishermen with equipment adapted to regional waters and seasonal conditions. ADVENT's maritime restrictions eventually reduced commercial fishing, but they continued producing nets for independent communities. When a resistance group needed to recover equipment from a flooded underground facility, they designed a reinforced retrieval net capable of carrying heavy machinery through narrow access tunnels. Their practical engineering skills attracted an XCOM quartermaster, who offered them a position in the resistance.

A former professional optometric technician from Cape Town, South Africa, this soldier specialized in repairing optical instruments and fitting corrective lenses. ADVENT's occupation introduced government-issued identification eyewear containing embedded electronic components. While servicing a damaged pair, they discovered that the device continuously transmitted visual information to an external receiver. They began warning clients against using the equipment and secretly removed several tracking components. A resistance scientist eventually recruited them to help investigate ADVENT surveillance technology and develop optical countermeasures.

This soldier had worked as a professional forest ecologist in the rural districts of Poland, studying woodland regeneration and wildlife habitats. ADVENT's occupation brought extensive industrial development into previously protected regions. During a survey, they discovered that several forest clearings contained evidence of alien excavation, although official maps identified the areas as untouched woodland. They began documenting the damage and tracking patrol movements through the surrounding forest. A resistance reconnaissance unit later recruited them for their knowledge of terrain, vegetation, and environmental changes.

Formerly a professional commercial baker in the outskirts of Istanbul, Turkey, this soldier operated an independent bakery supplying several residential districts. ADVENT's food distribution program eventually imposed strict production quotas, and their business was threatened with closure. They discovered that government inspectors were deliberately rejecting bread deliveries from independent bakeries to redirect customers toward centralized suppliers. They began distributing unsold products through an informal network serving displaced families. A resistance organizer who relied on the network later recruited them to coordinate provisions for underground safehouses.

This soldier had been a professional marine navigation instructor in the Philippines, teaching commercial sailors to operate older vessels without advanced electronic systems. ADVENT's occupation restricted independent maritime training, but they continued teaching privately to fishermen and coastal transport crews. When an ADVENT patrol disabled a local community's navigation equipment, they organized an improvised training program using traditional charts and celestial navigation. Several students subsequently joined a resistance maritime network and recommended their instructor for recruitment into XCOM.

A former professional medical prosthetist from Warsaw, Poland, this soldier specialized in designing artificial limbs for accident victims and injured workers. ADVENT's centralized medical system eventually replaced most independent prosthetic workshops, but they continued repairing older devices for residents unable to access government services. When a wounded resistance fighter arrived with an unfamiliar alien-made prosthesis, they discovered that the device contained a hidden monitoring system. They removed the component and contacted an underground medical group, which subsequently recruited them into XCOM's research and medical support personnel.

Before the invasion, this soldier worked as a commercial vineyard irrigation specialist in the rural districts of Portugal. Their expertise involved maintaining water systems and monitoring soil conditions across several wine-producing estates. ADVENT's agricultural authorities eventually introduced experimental treatments that increased yields but damaged traditional crops. They refused to implement the program and began helping independent growers preserve untreated vines. When government inspectors threatened to seize the vineyards, they organized an evacuation of the remaining seed stock. A resistance settlement later recruited them to manage its agricultural infrastructure.

This soldier had been a professional meteorite hunter in the deserts of Namibia, searching for rare extraterrestrial fragments and documenting impact sites. ADVENT's occupation initially left their work largely untouched, but government authorities eventually restricted access to several remote impact zones. During an unauthorized expedition, they discovered a meteorite containing an artificial structure that appeared to have been modified after landing. Their attempts to recover the object attracted an ADVENT security team. They escaped with several fragments and later joined a resistance scientific network that introduced them to XCOM.

A former professional stage illusionist from Prague, Czech Republic, this soldier specialized in sleight of hand and mechanical illusions. ADVENT's restrictions on public entertainment eventually forced them into private performances for wealthy collaborators. Their work occasionally brought them into government residences, where they learned to manipulate small security devices and conceal objects during inspections. After helping a resistance courier smuggle a data chip out of an administrative building, they were approached by an underground recruiter. Their unusual dexterity and ability to misdirect observers made them a useful XCOM recruit.

This soldier had worked as a commercial harbor dredging supervisor in the coastal regions of Chile. Their responsibilities included maintaining shipping channels and identifying submerged hazards. ADVENT's occupation expanded the port's military operations, and they began noticing that dredging schedules were being altered to conceal underwater construction. During an unauthorized inspection, they discovered an alien structure embedded in the harbor floor. They recorded its position and shared the information with a resistance maritime group. An XCOM officer later recruited them to assist with identifying submerged obstacles around occupied ports.

Formerly a professional instrument maker in the rural districts of Austria, this soldier specialized in constructing precision measuring devices for scientific laboratories. ADVENT's occupation initially brought lucrative government contracts, but they became suspicious when officials requested instruments calibrated to detect biological activity rather than physical measurements. Their investigation revealed that the devices were intended for use in tracking individuals carrying alien implants. They secretly altered the calibration equipment and supplied inaccurate readings to government facilities. After the sabotage was uncovered, a resistance scientist helped them escape and arranged their recruitment into XCOM.

Before the invasion, this soldier worked as a professional paper conservator in the archives of Florence, Italy. Their specialty was repairing water-damaged manuscripts and preserving fragile documents. When ADVENT began digitizing historical collections, they discovered that entire sections of local records were being quietly removed, including references to families who had vanished during early occupation sweeps. They concealed surviving originals inside restoration materials and passed copies to a network of underground historians. One of those historians later connected them with XCOM, where their patience and archival expertise proved useful in intelligence analysis.

This soldier had been a competitive sheepdog trial judge in the Welsh countryside, traveling between farms to evaluate working dogs. ADVENT's agricultural consolidation made independent competitions increasingly difficult, but they continued visiting isolated farms. During one trip, they noticed that a supposedly abandoned settlement was being used to hold displaced families. They coordinated a nighttime evacuation using familiar farm tracks and trained dogs to carry small supply bundles. A resistance organizer among the rescued families later recruited them to help guide patrols through rural terrain.

A former elevator maintenance inspector from Mexico City, this soldier understood the mechanical systems connecting the city's vast residential towers. ADVENT converted several high-rise buildings into controlled housing blocks, restricting movement between floors. When a fire trapped residents above a sealed security checkpoint, they bypassed the central controls and restored an emergency lift. Their intervention exposed an unauthorized detention level hidden beneath the building. After helping survivors reach a resistance safehouse, they were recruited to support urban rescue and infiltration missions.

This soldier had worked as a professional freshwater pearl cultivator in Lake Biwa, Japan. Their family business relied on carefully monitoring water quality and maintaining delicate mussel beds. After local authorities dismissed their findings, they helped a resistance scientific team retrieve evidence from the waterway. XCOM subsequently recruited them for aquatic reconnaissance and environmental analysis.

Before the occupation, this soldier worked as a professional locksmith specializing in antique mechanical locks in Tunis, Tunisia. This soldier had been a professional dairy fermentation specialist in the Swiss canton of Fribourg, developing cultures used in regional cheese production. A resistance supply coordinator recruited them to maintain food production for isolated settlements.

A former professional harbor pilot from Valparaíso, Chile, this soldier guided large vessels through difficult coastal approaches and crowded shipping channels. Suspecting concealed cargo, they deliberately delayed the ship until resistance observers could document its arrival. The resulting intelligence revealed a supply route for alien weapons. A local resistance commander subsequently recruited them to coordinate maritime operations.

This soldier had worked as a professional textile pattern grader in Manchester, England, adjusting clothing designs for different sizes and manufacturing specifications. When ADVENT introduced standardized uniforms, they were assigned to a government clothing contractor. They quietly altered production patterns to create extra internal pockets and hidden seams for resistance couriers. After an inspection uncovered one of the modifications, they escaped with a bundle of unfinished garments. A resistance quartermaster later recruited them to design concealed carrying equipment and civilian disguises.

Before the invasion, this soldier was a professional avalanche forecaster in the mountains of British Columbia, Canada. ADVENT's occupation brought military installations into several remote valleys, where heavy construction repeatedly disturbed the surrounding terrain. They noticed that an unusual pattern of blasting was creating dangerous avalanche conditions above a settlement. When officials ignored their warnings, they organized an evacuation and led residents through a safer route. A resistance mountain unit recruited them for their knowledge of snow and terrain.

This soldier had been a professional puppeteer in Marrakesh, Morocco, performing traditional shadow theater for local audiences. ADVENT restricted public gatherings, but small performances continued in private courtyards. They began using changes in puppet movements and lighting to signal warnings to nearby resistance sympathizers. When a performance was interrupted by a security patrol, they hid several couriers among the departing audience. One of those couriers later introduced them to an underground communications group, which recruited them to help coordinate covert messages.

A former professional elevator shaft surveyor from Hong Kong, this soldier specialized in inspecting structural alignment in densely built commercial towers. During an inspection, they discovered a sealed shaft descending far below the building's official foundations. The shaft contained equipment used to move detainees between hidden levels. They copied the structural plans and passed them to a resistance cell, which later recruited them to identify concealed routes through occupied buildings.

This soldier had worked as a professional medicinal plant grower in the highlands of Guatemala, cultivating traditional herbs for local clinics. ADVENT's centralized healthcare system restricted access to many independent remedies, especially in remote communities. When a government medical convoy stopped supplying a mountain settlement, they organized a network of growers to produce basic treatments and distribute them discreetly. Their knowledge became especially valuable after several residents were injured during a resistance evacuation. An XCOM medical officer later recruited them to support field medicine and botanical research.

Before the invasion, this soldier worked as a professional theater acoustician in Vienna, Austria, designing sound systems for concert halls and opera houses. ADVENT's occupation repurposed several cultural buildings for government ceremonies, but they remained employed maintaining the equipment. They discovered that a public address system had been modified to broadcast inaudible signals that interfered with nearby civilian communications. They documented the frequency pattern and supplied it to a resistance radio operator. Their expertise helped XCOM develop countermeasures, and they were recruited to assist with electronic warfare.

This soldier had been a professional commercial mushroom cultivator in the caves beneath the Dordogne region of France. Their underground growing operation used carefully controlled humidity and temperature to produce specialty crops. When ADVENT began using nearby caves for waste disposal, they noticed that unfamiliar spores were spreading through the ventilation channels. They traced the contamination to discarded alien biological material and warned neighboring settlements before anyone became seriously ill. A resistance scientist recruited them to help identify and contain fungal hazards associated with alien facilities.

A former professional boatbuilder from the Mekong Delta in Vietnam, this soldier constructed shallow-draft vessels suited to flooded farmland and narrow waterways. ADVENT's occupation introduced patrol craft that struggled to navigate the region's smaller channels. They began quietly modifying local boats to carry more supplies while producing less noise. When a resistance group needed to evacuate a village surrounded by patrols, they designed a route through irrigation channels that larger vessels could not follow. Their success led to recruitment as a specialist in riverine operations.

This soldier had worked as a professional braille transcriptionist in Dublin, Ireland, producing accessible documents for blind readers. ADVENT's information controls eventually restricted independent publishing, but they continued transcribing materials for private clients. A resistance organizer approached them with intercepted government schedules and asked for a format that could be carried without attracting attention. They developed a compact tactile code that allowed couriers to memorize information through touch. When the network was compromised, they helped preserve its records and were recruited into XCOM's communications section.

Before the invasion, this soldier was a professional mining ventilation engineer in the copper districts of Zambia. Their work involved maintaining airflow and monitoring dangerous gases in underground shafts. ADVENT's expansion brought automated excavation equipment into the region, but several tunnels began experiencing unexplained pressure changes. They discovered that alien machinery had connected the old mine network to a deeper underground facility. When a collapse trapped a group of workers, they opened an alternate ventilation route and guided rescuers inside. A resistance engineering team later recruited them for subterranean operations.

This soldier had been a professional beekeeper's equipment manufacturer in Ljubljana, Slovenia, producing hives, protective clothing, and extraction tools. ADVENT's agricultural policies disrupted traditional pollination, but their workshop remained active through rural customers. They began modifying hive boxes to conceal small radio components and emergency supplies for resistance couriers. When a patrol searched their premises, several devices were carried out unnoticed inside ordinary equipment shipments. A resistance quartermaster eventually recruited them to manufacture discreet field gear and maintain supply links between isolated communities.

A former professional marine mammal acoustics researcher from the Azores, Portugal, this soldier studied whale and dolphin communication. Their recordings began capturing repeated low-frequency signals that did not match any known marine species. They identified the source as an alien underwater installation and shared the analysis with an independent oceanographic group. After a resistance team confirmed the site, XCOM recruited them to monitor submerged alien activity and interpret unusual acoustic transmissions.

This soldier had worked as a professional locksmithing instructor in the industrial city of Brno, Czech Republic. Their courses emphasized mechanical security, safe handling, and emergency access. Instead, they quietly instructed maintenance workers in ways to open locked rooms during emergencies. After helping several prisoners escape a temporary holding center, they were recruited by a resistance cell as a specialist in mechanical entry.

Before the invasion, this soldier worked as a professional cartographic typesetter in Reykjavík, Iceland, preparing maps and navigational charts for maritime publishers. They preserved the original survey plates and reproduced accurate maps for resistance travelers. An XCOM scout later recruited them to maintain field maps and update navigation records in contested regions.

This soldier had been a professional medical equipment sterilization technician in Accra, Ghana. Their work involved maintaining infection-control standards in hospitals and mobile clinics. Their investigation revealed an unauthorized program involving alien implants. They copied the treatment logs and helped several patients escape before the next scheduled procedure. A resistance physician later recruited them for medical support and biological containment work.

A former professional falconry veterinarian from the outskirts of Amman, Jordan, this soldier treated injuries in hunting and racing birds. ADVENT's occupation limited traditional falconry gatherings, but private breeders continued seeking their services. During a treatment session, they discovered an unusual tracking implant beneath the feathers of a bird returned from a restricted government estate. They removed it and traced its signal to a nearby communications post. A resistance scout used the information to identify a surveillance network and subsequently recruited them for animal-assisted reconnaissance.

This soldier had worked as a professional precision glass cutter in the industrial districts of Alexandria, Egypt. Their workshop supplied laboratories, hospitals, and architectural restoration projects. ADVENT's authorities eventually required special permits for optical glass, but they continued producing custom components through private orders. A resistance scientist asked them to fabricate a set of lenses for examining alien materials without direct exposure. Their careful work helped identify a previously unknown weakness in a protective casing, earning them an invitation to join an XCOM technical team.

Before the occupation, this soldier was a professional dairy herd geneticist in the Waikato region of New Zealand. This soldier had been a professional museum lighting technician in St. Petersburg, Russia. A former professional underwater photographer from the Red Sea coast of Egypt, this soldier documented shipwrecks and coral habitats for scientific publications. Beneath the wreck, they captured images of an alien device attached to the seabed. Security personnel seized their equipment, but they had already transmitted the photographs to a resistance contact. Their underwater experience led to recruitment by an XCOM team investigating submerged installations.

This soldier had worked as a professional industrial laundry supervisor in the suburbs of Paris, France. When they discovered that the ward was connected to an alien medical program, they passed their evidence to a resistance physician, who arranged their recruitment into XCOM's intelligence support staff.

Before the invasion, this soldier worked as a professional commercial glider instructor in the Czech countryside. They taught students to fly using thermals and careful observation of local weather. When a resistance courier was stranded beyond a patrol line, they used a glider to deliver emergency supplies and guide the courier toward safety. This soldier had been a professional stone mason in the ancient districts of Petra, Jordan, restoring damaged facades and carved structures. While repairing a collapsed passage, they discovered a sealed chamber containing evidence of an earlier resistance hiding place. They delivered the records to a local underground group, which later recruited them to construct concealed shelters.

A former professional coffee quality grader from the highlands of Honduras, this soldier evaluated bean samples for export cooperatives. When a group of escaped experimental creatures began appearing near a settlement, they recognized signs of stress conditioning and predicted where the animals would seek shelter. Before the invasion, this soldier was a professional commercial diving instructor in the coastal waters of Croatia. Their work involved teaching safe underwater navigation and emergency procedures. After discovering that patrols were guarding an underwater entrance near an old naval tunnel, they mapped an alternate route through a submerged cavern. A resistance team used the passage to recover trapped operatives, and the instructor was subsequently recruited for underwater reconnaissance.

This soldier had been a professional musical instrument tuner in New Orleans, Louisiana. They traveled between schools, churches, and performance halls, maintaining pianos and other instruments. A resistance communications specialist recruited them to identify covert listening devices and maintain discreet signal equipment.

A former professional saltwater aquarist from Okinawa, Japan, this soldier maintained marine exhibits and researched coral propagation. This soldier had worked as a professional theatrical costume dyer in Kolkata, India, producing fabrics for traditional performances and commercial productions. They developed a series of reversible dyes that allowed resistance couriers to alter clothing colors quickly without carrying spare garments. Before the invasion, this soldier worked as a professional railway bridge maintenance diver in the Danube region of Romania. This soldier had been a professional seed bank curator in the rural districts of Norway, preserving rare crop varieties for agricultural research. An XCOM logistics officer recruited them to support agricultural resilience across liberated communities.

A former professional industrial photographer from Detroit, Michigan, this soldier documented factory equipment, production processes, and workplace safety conditions. This soldier had worked as a professional mountaineering equipment repairer in the Italian Alps. Their workshop serviced climbing harnesses, ropes, crampons, and expedition hardware. This soldier had been a professional traditional boat caulker in the coastal districts of Kerala, India. Their craft involved sealing wooden vessels with natural fibers and waterproof compounds. A former professional industrial refrigeration designer from Monterrey, Mexico, this soldier specialized in cooling systems for food warehouses and manufacturing plants. When an alien power station disrupted the local drainage controls, they organized residents to open manual floodgates and protect an evacuation route. A former professional mountain botanist from the Caucasus region of Georgia, this soldier studied alpine plants and their adaptation to extreme conditions. This soldier had worked as a professional clockmaker in the old city of Fez, Morocco, restoring mechanical timepieces and constructing custom movements. Before the invasion, this soldier worked as a professional emergency dispatcher in Christchurch, New Zealand, coordinating fire, ambulance, and rescue responses. This soldier had been a professional industrial diamond cutter in Antwerp, Belgium, working with precision tools and high-value materials. A resistance engineer used the findings to develop a countermeasure and recruited them into XCOM's technical division.

Before the invasion, this soldier worked as a professional paper marbler in Istanbul, Turkey, creating decorative patterns for book covers and official documents. This soldier had been a professional volcanic observatory technician in southern Iceland, maintaining instruments that monitored seismic activity and gas emissions. After an ADVENT patrol attempted to seize the equipment, they escaped and joined an XCOM geological reconnaissance team.

A former professional sign language interpreter from Nairobi, Kenya, this soldier worked in schools and public institutions serving deaf communities. A resistance organizer later recruited them to coordinate discreet communication among civilians and field operatives.

This soldier had worked as a professional industrial chimney inspector in Glasgow, Scotland, examining tall stacks and identifying structural hazards. Before the invasion, this soldier worked as a professional cheese-ripening consultant in the French Jura, advising small producers on temperature, humidity, and storage conditions. This soldier had been a professional archaeological photographer in Luxor, Egypt, documenting excavation sites and fragile wall paintings. A former professional ice cream refrigeration technician from Buenos Aires, Argentina, this soldier maintained freezing equipment for independent food shops. When a resistance medical team needed to transport temperature-sensitive samples across the city, they modified a delivery freezer to operate without its normal electrical supply. This soldier had worked as a professional landscape irrigation designer in the arid regions of Morocco, creating water-efficient gardens for public spaces and private estates. Before the invasion, this soldier was a professional veterinary radiographer in Perth, Australia, specializing in diagnostic imaging for large animals. This soldier had been a professional paper mill engineer in the forests of central Finland, overseeing the production of pulp and recycled paper. A former professional traditional dance instructor from Dakar, Senegal, this soldier taught regional dance and percussion to students of all ages. This soldier had worked as a professional railway tunnel ventilation specialist in the Alps of northern Italy. Before the invasion, this soldier worked as a professional seed potato inspector in the rural districts of Scotland. A former professional court sketch artist from New York City, this soldier had spent years documenting trials and legal proceedings through quick drawings. Before the invasion, this soldier was a professional theatrical rigging inspector in London, England, responsible for checking suspended scenery, counterweights, and safety lines. They collected a sample and disabled the circuit before it could cause a dangerous pressure surge. A resistance engineer later recruited them to investigate alien machinery and industrial hazards.

Before the invasion, this soldier was a professional rural midwife in the highlands of Ethiopia, serving families in communities far from major hospitals. When an ADVENT relocation sweep threatened several families, they organized a temporary shelter for expectant mothers and children. A resistance medic who encountered the shelter recruited them into an XCOM-supported medical network.

This soldier had been a professional commercial diving photographer in the waters around Bermuda, documenting underwater construction and marine research. Their experience documenting underwater structures made them a valuable recruit for an XCOM team investigating alien installations below the surface.

A former professional leather bookbinder in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, this soldier specialized in repairing damaged books and restoring handwritten records. ADVENT's occupation brought censorship to libraries and private collections, and they began preserving banned texts inside the covers of harmless government manuals. A resistance archivist later recruited them to preserve intelligence and maintain underground libraries.

This soldier had worked as a professional horticultural lighting technician in the Netherlands, designing artificial light systems for commercial greenhouses. A resistance scientist recruited them to investigate environmental manipulation and develop countermeasures.

Before the invasion, this soldier worked as a professional marine salvage estimator in the port of Thessaloniki, Greece. Their knowledge of salvage operations earned them recruitment into XCOM's recovery section.

This soldier had been a professional traditional instrument restorer in Oaxaca, Mexico, repairing wooden drums and string instruments used in regional music. This soldier had worked as a professional commercial bread oven engineer in Istanbul, Turkey, designing and maintaining high-capacity baking equipment. The resistance group later recruited them to help plan industrial diversions and maintain equipment in safehouses.
