Their work attracted an XCOM quartermaster, who recruited them to manufacture field uniforms and equipment covers.

Before the invasion, this soldier was a professional alpine lake limnologist in the Italian Dolomites, studying freshwater chemistry and aquatic ecosystems. ADVENT's occupation established restricted facilities near several lakes, and their samples began showing unusual mineral deposits and temperature changes. They traced the disturbance to an alien power system buried beneath the lakebed. Their warning helped a resistance team avoid a contaminated shoreline. XCOM recruited them to monitor freshwater environments and assess the ecological effects of alien installations.

This soldier had been a professional antique map restorer in Seville, Spain, repairing navigational charts and historical land surveys. ADVENT's occupation restricted access to private archives, but they continued working for a small museum. A damaged map brought in for restoration contained an unusual layer of ink that became visible under ultraviolet light. The hidden markings identified a network of safehouses established during the first years of occupation. They passed the information to a resistance historian, who recruited them to authenticate documents and recover lost intelligence.

A former professional industrial fire suppression technician in the refineries of Kuwait, this soldier maintained automatic systems designed to contain fuel and chemical fires. ADVENT's occupation brought new energy facilities into the region, and they discovered that several fire suppression systems had been disabled in buildings used for human experimentation. They restored the equipment and triggered a false alarm that forced an evacuation. Several detainees escaped through the service corridors. A resistance engineer later recruited them to sabotage hazardous facilities and protect underground laboratories.

This soldier had worked as a professional traditional silk reeler in the rural districts of Vietnam, processing cocoons into fine thread for local weaving cooperatives. ADVENT's industrial policies threatened the traditional silk trade, but they continued operating a small workshop. They discovered that a government textile plant was using an alien-derived treatment that weakened the surrounding mulberry crops. They preserved healthy silkworm stock and warned neighboring growers. A resistance agricultural group later recruited them to maintain local production and investigate biological contamination.

Before the invasion, this soldier was a professional railway timetable compiler in Belgrade, Serbia, coordinating schedules across regional passenger and freight routes. ADVENT's occupation centralized transport records, but they noticed repeated discrepancies between published schedules and actual military movements. By comparing archived timetables with station reports, they identified a hidden prisoner transport pattern. They leaked the information to a resistance cell, allowing several families to intercept a transfer and free detainees. XCOM recruited them to analyze logistics networks and predict enemy movements.

This soldier had been a professional industrial ceramic sensor technician in the manufacturing districts of Yokohama, Japan. Their work involved producing heat-resistant components for precision instruments. ADVENT's factories began ordering unusual ceramic elements designed to operate inside alien power systems. They discovered that the components emitted a faint pulse when exposed to certain electromagnetic frequencies. Rather than complete the contract, they preserved the test results and gave them to a resistance engineer. Their discovery helped XCOM identify a weakness in alien equipment, and they were recruited into its research division.

Before the invasion, this soldier worked as a professional avalanche-control explosives technician in the mountains of northern Italy. They had spent years managing controlled detonations to protect roads and ski villages. When ADVENT established a mountain listening post, its construction destabilized a nearby slope. They warned officials, but the warning was ignored. After a patrol was buried by a naturally occurring slide, they used their expertise to open a safe passage for trapped civilians. A resistance commander recruited them for demolition and mountain operations.

This soldier had been a professional puppeteer in the coastal city of Essaouira, Morocco, performing traditional shadow plays for children and tourists. ADVENT's occupation restricted public gatherings, so they began staging private performances in family courtyards. Their moving silhouettes provided cover for couriers exchanging messages behind the screen. When a young performer was detained, they organized a distraction that helped the child escape. A resistance organizer subsequently recruited them to coordinate diversions and clandestine meetings.

A former professional meteorite curator from the Atacama region of Chile, this soldier had catalogued fragments collected by desert researchers. During the occupation, an ADVENT survey team confiscated several specimens after detecting unusual traces within them. They recognized that one fragment matched material recovered near a concealed alien excavation. Rather than surrender their remaining records, they hid the catalogue in a remote observatory. An XCOM scientist eventually located them and recruited them to identify extraterrestrial materials.

This soldier had worked as a professional chimney sweep in the old neighborhoods of Istanbul, maintaining flues in densely packed residential buildings. ADVENT's surveillance network overlooked many older ventilation systems, and they learned to move between rooftops without crossing monitored streets. When a family was trapped during a building search, they guided them through adjoining chimneys and service passages. A local resistance cell offered them shelter afterward and recruited them to map concealed routes through occupied districts.

Before the invasion, this soldier was a professional seed-cleaning machine operator in the agricultural plains of Saskatchewan, Canada. They separated viable grain from damaged or contaminated harvests at a cooperative facility. ADVENT's food authorities began rejecting locally grown crops without explanation, and they discovered that the rejection tests had been deliberately calibrated to favor government-controlled seed stock. They preserved untreated grain and helped farmers establish an independent supply. A resistance quartermaster recruited them to manage food reserves.

This soldier had been a professional stage illusion designer in Macau, creating mechanical effects for theaters and touring performers. After ADVENT banned many public shows, they converted their workshop into a repair business. A resistance courier approached them seeking a way to conceal a person-sized compartment inside a delivery cart. Their design successfully moved an injured operative through a checkpoint. Impressed by their practical ingenuity, the courier's handler recruited them to develop concealment devices and extraction equipment.

A former professional salt-marsh restoration specialist from the Camargue region of France, this soldier had worked to protect wetlands and their wildlife. ADVENT's coastal development projects redirected waterways and damaged several protected habitats. While documenting the destruction, they discovered that a new drainage channel concealed an underground power conduit leading to an alien facility. They guided local residents through the marshes when patrols arrived. A resistance scout recruited them for navigation and environmental reconnaissance.

This soldier had worked as a professional dental prosthetics technician in the city of Córdoba, Argentina, producing custom devices for patients who had lost teeth or suffered facial injuries. ADVENT's medical system increasingly denied treatment to unregistered civilians. They began repairing prosthetics without official records and provided free work to displaced families. When a resistance medic needed a replacement jaw component for an injured operative, they produced one using salvaged materials. The medic later recruited them to support field hospitals and casualty recovery.

Before the invasion, this soldier was a professional railway tunnel ventilation inspector in the mountains of Austria. Their work involved testing airflow and emergency extraction systems in long underground passages. ADVENT repurposed several tunnels for military transport, but they discovered that one had been sealed with workers still inside. They bypassed the ventilation controls and established an air supply long enough for the trapped crew to escape. A resistance engineer recruited them to assess underground facilities and plan tunnel-based operations.

This soldier had been a professional traditional paper umbrella maker in Kyoto, Japan, crafting lightweight frames and weatherproof coverings. ADVENT's occupation reduced demand for handmade goods, but they continued working from a small family shop. They began hiding handwritten messages beneath the replaceable paper layers of umbrellas sold near government offices. A resistance courier discovered the method and used it to transmit checkpoint schedules. The courier eventually recruited them to maintain a discreet civilian communications network.

A former professional volcanic gas monitor from the island of Java, Indonesia, this soldier had maintained sensors near active volcanic vents. During the occupation, unusual readings appeared around an ADVENT geological installation built on an inactive volcanic slope. Their instruments detected compounds that did not match any known volcanic source. When they attempted to report the anomaly, officials confiscated their equipment. They escaped with a handwritten record of the readings and were recruited by XCOM to monitor alien emissions.

This soldier had worked as a professional racing pigeon breeder in the outskirts of Brussels, Belgium. They specialized in training birds to navigate long distances and return to unfamiliar lofts. ADVENT's communications restrictions made traditional message delivery unexpectedly valuable. They began carrying short coded notes between isolated resistance groups, using routes that avoided major checkpoints. After several birds failed to return, they discovered a government transmitter was interfering with their navigation. A resistance intelligence officer recruited them to develop alternative courier routes.

Before the invasion, this soldier was a professional stone conservator in the ancient city of Petra, Jordan, repairing weathered carvings and protecting fragile structures. ADVENT's occupation placed the archaeological site under military control, and they were ordered to seal an underground chamber uncovered by construction crews. Inside, they found evidence of an alien device embedded in the bedrock. They concealed photographs and samples before the chamber was closed. A resistance historian passed the evidence to XCOM, which recruited them for archaeological reconnaissance.

This soldier had been a professional industrial laundry engineer in the textile districts of Lahore, Pakistan. They maintained large washing systems used by hospitals, hotels, and factories. ADVENT's occupation introduced a new uniform-cleaning process that left a persistent chemical residue on clothing. Their tests showed that the residue could interfere with certain electronic sensors. They shared the discovery with a resistance technician, who used it to obscure a courier's tracking tag. XCOM later recruited them to develop practical counter-surveillance materials.

A former professional sea turtle conservation officer from the beaches of Costa Rica, this soldier had monitored nesting sites and protected hatchlings from poachers. ADVENT's coastal patrols disrupted nesting seasons, and their new security lights caused hatchlings to become disoriented. They organized volunteers to relocate vulnerable nests and documented the effects of the lighting system. When officials ordered the beach closed, a resistance group helped them continue the work from a hidden camp. They were later recruited to support coastal environmental intelligence.

This soldier had worked as a professional industrial boiler water chemist in the steelworks of Ostrava, Czech Republic. They tested water quality to prevent corrosion and dangerous pressure failures. ADVENT's new power facilities used unfamiliar cooling systems, and their samples revealed a metallic compound that reacted with standard treatment chemicals. They traced the contamination to an alien reactor component and quietly shared the results with a resistance engineer. Their expertise helped disable a failing generator before it exploded, earning them recruitment into XCOM.

Before the invasion, this soldier was a professional traditional reed instrument maker in the marshlands of Iraq, crafting flutes and pipes from locally harvested reeds. ADVENT's occupation displaced many communities along the waterways, but they continued gathering materials in remote wetlands. They used their regular boat journeys to carry medicine and messages between isolated settlements. When a patrol seized their vessel, they escaped through narrow reed channels known only to local fishermen. A resistance network recruited them as a guide and supply runner.

This soldier had been a professional industrial color-matching technician in the automotive plants of Turin, Italy. They specialized in reproducing precise paint finishes for vehicle production. ADVENT's military contractors began ordering coatings that absorbed unusual wavelengths of light, and they discovered the material was intended for alien stealth equipment. They copied the formula and passed it to a resistance laboratory before abandoning their position. Their knowledge of pigments and surface treatments later earned them a place in XCOM's camouflage development section.

A former professional cave hydrologist from the karst regions of Slovenia, this soldier studied underground rivers and freshwater reserves. ADVENT's occupation brought drilling crews into protected cave systems, where they discovered that an underground stream had been redirected toward a concealed installation. They mapped an alternative watercourse and helped nearby villages avoid losing their supply. When the drilling operation expanded, they led a resistance team through the cave network to destroy its pumping equipment. XCOM recruited them for subterranean reconnaissance.

This soldier had worked as a professional theatrical wig maker in London, creating realistic hairpieces for stage and screen productions. ADVENT's occupation turned many theaters into government venues, but they continued accepting private commissions. They began producing convincing disguises for resistance couriers who needed to change their appearance quickly. One courier used a specially prepared wig to escape a city checkpoint after being recognized. The resistance cell later recruited them to assist with identity concealment and infiltration preparation.

Before the invasion, this soldier was a professional glacier cave guide in Iceland, leading expeditions through unstable ice formations. ADVENT's occupation brought geological researchers into the region, and they noticed unusual warmth and artificial light beneath a remote glacier. During an unauthorized survey, they discovered an alien drilling chamber that was melting the surrounding ice. They guided a group of displaced researchers to safety through a secondary cave entrance. XCOM recruited them for their expertise in hazardous frozen terrain.

This soldier had been a professional traditional basketry teacher in the highlands of Rwanda, passing on techniques for weaving durable containers from local fibers. ADVENT's ration system introduced standardized packaging that often failed during transport over rough terrain. They began producing reinforced baskets for a rural resistance clinic, allowing medicine to be carried safely without attracting attention. When the clinic was relocated after a raid, their containers helped move its supplies through dense forest. A resistance quartermaster recruited them to improve field logistics.

A former professional industrial acoustic engineer in the shipyards of Gdynia, Poland, this soldier specialized in reducing vibration and noise aboard large vessels. ADVENT's naval contractors installed unfamiliar propulsion systems, and they discovered that the machinery produced a low-frequency signal that affected nearby civilian equipment. They traced the source to an alien power coupling and recorded its operating pattern. A resistance technician used the data to disrupt a harbor patrol's sensors. XCOM subsequently recruited them to analyze enemy machinery and develop countermeasures.

This soldier had worked as a professional desert irrigation surveyor in the oases of southern Morocco. They mapped ancient channels and maintained systems that carried water to remote farms. ADVENT's occupation diverted several springs toward a military installation, threatening entire communities. They secretly reopened a disused underground channel and restored water to a settlement before government crews arrived. The villagers sheltered them when their work was discovered, and a resistance organizer later recruited them to support operations in arid terrain.

Before the invasion, this soldier was a professional traditional bell foundry technician in the mountains of northern Portugal. They maintained casting equipment and repaired bells for churches and civic buildings. ADVENT's occupation restricted public ceremonies, but the foundry remained open under government contract. They discovered that a shipment of metal intended for a military communications tower contained an unusual alloy that distorted radio signals. They saved a sample and delivered it to a resistance engineer, who recruited them to develop signal-disruption equipment.

This soldier had been a professional wildlife disease diagnostician in the grasslands of Botswana, examining samples from livestock and wild animals. ADVENT's occupation introduced a new veterinary surveillance program, and they noticed that several supposedly unrelated animal deaths shared the same neurological symptoms. Their investigation revealed an alien pathogen spreading through contaminated feed. They warned local herders and preserved samples before the authorities could confiscate them. An XCOM medical researcher recruited them to assist with xenobiological disease analysis.

A former professional theatrical fire-effects operator in the city of Manila, Philippines, this soldier had designed controlled flames and smoke effects for live performances. ADVENT's occupation shut down most entertainment venues, but their equipment remained useful to resistance groups. They modified a portable smoke generator to produce a dense screen without toxic chemicals. During a raid on a safehouse, the device concealed the evacuation of several civilians. A resistance field leader recruited them to develop nonlethal diversions and battlefield concealment systems.

This soldier had worked as a professional railway wheel inspector in the industrial districts of Katowice, Poland. They used precision instruments to detect cracks and uneven wear before trains could be returned to service. ADVENT's military transport schedules left little time for proper inspections, and they discovered that several freight cars had dangerous structural defects. Rather than approve them, they reported the faults and delayed a shipment carrying alien equipment. A resistance operative later recruited them to identify weaknesses in enemy transport systems.

Before the invasion, this soldier was a professional traditional barkcloth maker in Uganda, producing durable fabric from the inner bark of native trees. ADVENT's occupation threatened the forests used for their craft, but they continued working with a small community cooperative. They began using layered barkcloth to conceal thin maps and written instructions inside ordinary market goods. When a courier was searched, the concealed material remained unnoticed. A resistance organizer recruited them to create low-tech concealment methods for civilian networks.

This soldier had been a professional high-altitude balloon meteorologist in the Andes of Bolivia, launching instruments to study atmospheric conditions. ADVENT's occupation established a communications station near their former launch site, and their weather balloons began returning with unexplained interference patterns. They tracked the signal to an alien relay hidden above the cloud line. Their report reached an XCOM research team through a resistance radio operator, and they were recruited to help monitor atmospheric disturbances and high-altitude installations.

A former professional ship's provision auditor in the port of Piraeus, Greece, this soldier checked food, fuel, and medical inventories aboard commercial vessels. ADVENT's occupation imposed strict cargo controls, but they noticed that several ships were recording supplies that never reached their destinations. The missing goods were being diverted to a covert detention facility. They copied the manifests and passed them to a resistance group, which used the information to intercept a shipment. Their accounting expertise earned them recruitment into resistance logistics.

This soldier had worked as a professional industrial leather chemist in the manufacturing districts of León, Mexico. They developed treatments that made leather more durable and resistant to heat and moisture. ADVENT's contractors requested a new coating for military equipment, but their tests revealed that the treatment contained a substance derived from alien tissue. They refused to approve the formula and secretly preserved the samples. A resistance laboratory used their findings to identify contaminated materials, then recruited them to develop safer protective gear.

Before the invasion, this soldier was a professional traditional wooden boat caulker in the fishing villages of Brittany, France. They sealed hulls using fibers and natural compounds, keeping small vessels seaworthy in rough coastal waters. ADVENT's maritime restrictions made it difficult for fishing communities to travel, but they helped several families repair boats used for clandestine crossings. After guiding an injured resistance courier to a hidden harbor, they were recruited to maintain small transport craft and plan coastal escapes.

This soldier had been a professional industrial paper recycling technician in the outskirts of Helsinki, Finland. They operated machinery that separated ink, plastic, and other contaminants from waste paper. ADVENT's occupation introduced a new recycling process that destroyed documents containing certain classified markings. They discovered that the machinery was being used to erase records from confiscated archives. They secretly recovered several damaged files and passed them to a resistance historian, who recruited them to preserve evidence and recover destroyed information.

A former professional cave diving instructor from the Yucatán Peninsula, Mexico, this soldier trained divers to navigate flooded underground passages. ADVENT's occupation restricted access to several cenotes after military researchers discovered unusual structures beneath the water. They guided a resistance team through a secondary cave system to retrieve equipment abandoned by an earlier expedition. When a security drone entered the passage, they led the team through a narrow submerged route that avoided detection. XCOM later recruited them for aquatic infiltration.

This soldier had worked as a professional industrial refrigeration controls programmer in the food-processing districts of Rosario, Argentina. They maintained automated systems that regulated temperature across large storage facilities. ADVENT's occupation brought new government installations under their supervision, and they discovered that a cold-storage complex was actually maintaining an alien biological specimen. They altered the controls to prevent a planned transfer and alerted a resistance scientist. After escaping the facility, they were recruited to support XCOM containment and equipment systems.

Before the invasion, this soldier was a professional traditional woodblock printer in the city of Luang Prabang, Laos. They produced illustrations and educational materials for local schools and cultural organizations. ADVENT's occupation restricted independent publishing, but they continued printing small editions for village teachers. They began hiding resistance instructions within apparently ordinary illustrations, using tiny changes in borders and decorative motifs. When a school network successfully passed several messages, a resistance liaison recruited them to maintain covert print communications.

This soldier had been a professional industrial pipeline corrosion specialist in the oil fields of Alberta, Canada. They inspected long-distance pipelines and assessed damage caused by pressure, weather, and chemical exposure. ADVENT's occupation introduced an unfamiliar coating to several military fuel lines, and their tests revealed that the material concealed a network of alien sensors. They mapped the affected sections and gave the findings to a resistance engineer. XCOM recruited them to identify concealed infrastructure and disable enemy supply systems.

A former professional mountain orchard pollination manager from the valleys of Kyrgyzstan, this soldier coordinated seasonal work to maintain fruit production in remote communities. ADVENT's agricultural program introduced artificial pollination drones that displaced local workers and damaged several traditional orchards. They organized growers to restore manual pollination and protect native varieties. When a government patrol attempted to seize their stored seeds, neighboring farmers helped them escape through the hills. A resistance quartermaster recruited them to support rural food production.

This soldier had worked as a professional traditional instrument restorer in the city of Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, repairing historic lutes, drums, and string instruments. ADVENT's occupation forced many cultural institutions to close, but they continued restoring privately owned instruments. A damaged drum brought to their workshop contained a small data chip hidden beneath its internal brace. They traced the owner to a missing resistance musician and delivered the chip to a surviving contact. The contact later recruited them to recover concealed intelligence.

Before the invasion, this soldier was a professional industrial desalination plant operator in Muscat, Oman. They managed filtration systems that supplied drinking water to coastal communities. ADVENT's occupation placed the plant under military administration, and they discovered that a new intake system was drawing contaminated water toward a civilian reservoir. They shut down the affected line despite orders to keep production running, preventing widespread illness. A resistance medical team helped them evade arrest and recruited them to maintain independent water supplies.

This soldier had been a professional traditional stained-glass painter in the city of Puebla, Mexico, creating decorative panels for historic buildings. ADVENT's occupation brought restrictions on religious gatherings, and several buildings were converted into administrative centers. While repairing a confiscated window, they discovered that earlier restorers had hidden a coded list of missing civilians inside the leadwork. They preserved the information and delivered it to a resistance archivist. Their careful hands and knowledge of historic structures later earned them recruitment into XCOM.

A former professional industrial crane load assessor in the port of Durban, South Africa, this soldier calculated safe lifting limits for heavy cargo. ADVENT's occupation increased military shipping activity, and they discovered that several containers were being moved under false weight declarations. Their calculations showed that the loads contained dense alien machinery concealed beneath ordinary freight. They copied the shipping records and passed them to a resistance dockworker, helping expose a covert supply route. An XCOM logistics officer recruited them to assess enemy cargo movements.

This soldier had worked as a professional traditional felt maker in the mountains of Mongolia, producing warm clothing and insulation from sheep's wool. ADVENT's occupation disrupted pastoral communities, but they continued supplying families displaced from their grazing lands. They developed compact felt shelters that could be assembled quickly and insulated against severe cold. A resistance patrol used the shelters during a winter evacuation, allowing wounded civilians to survive overnight. The patrol commander later recruited them to improve field shelter and cold-weather equipment.

Before the invasion, this soldier was a professional industrial laser alignment technician in the manufacturing districts of Singapore. They calibrated precision equipment used in electronics production. ADVENT's factories introduced unfamiliar laser systems that repeatedly drifted from their programmed settings. Their inspection revealed that the devices were being used to map human movement through reflections from building surfaces. They copied the calibration data and provided it to a resistance technician, who developed a way to disrupt the system. XCOM recruited them for precision optics and sensor countermeasures.

This soldier had been a professional traditional salt-pan supervisor in the coastal wetlands of Senegal, managing evaporation ponds and coordinating seasonal harvests. ADVENT's occupation restricted access to the shoreline, and military construction threatened the local salt industry. They organized workers to move supplies through abandoned ponds and raised embankments, avoiding patrol roads. When a resistance group needed a concealed crossing during a coastal evacuation, they provided a safe route. Their knowledge of tides and terrain earned them recruitment as a field guide.

A former professional industrial textile testing technician in the city of Bursa, Turkey, this soldier examined fabric for strength, fire resistance, and chemical durability. ADVENT's occupation brought orders for new uniforms made from an unfamiliar synthetic fiber. Their tests showed that the material reacted to alien energy emissions and became brittle after prolonged exposure. They quietly shared the results with a resistance quartermaster, preventing several units from relying on defective equipment. XCOM recruited them to test armor fabrics and protective materials.

This soldier had worked as a professional traditional stone irrigation channel mason in the highlands of Peru. They repaired ancient terraces and maintained narrow watercourses used by remote farming communities. ADVENT's occupation redirected water toward a military settlement, leaving several villages without reliable irrigation. They helped local farmers restore an older channel system hidden beneath collapsed stonework. When patrols arrived, the villagers concealed them in an abandoned terrace storehouse. A resistance organizer later recruited them to maintain rural supply routes.

Before the invasion, this soldier was a professional industrial acoustic leak detector in the suburbs of Melbourne, Australia. They used sensitive microphones to locate faults in underground water and gas pipes. ADVENT's occupation brought extensive construction beneath the city, and they detected a repeating vibration that did not match any known utility system. Following the signal, they found a concealed alien transit conduit beneath a government building. They provided the location to XCOM and were recruited to help locate hidden underground infrastructure.

This soldier had been a professional traditional bookbinder in the city of Fez, Morocco, repairing manuscripts and producing hand-bound volumes for private collectors. ADVENT's occupation placed many libraries under government supervision, but they continued restoring books in a small workshop. While repairing a damaged volume, they discovered a series of handwritten notes identifying civilians who had secretly assisted the resistance during the earliest days of occupation. They delivered the names to a surviving organizer, who recruited them to preserve the network's history and help rebuild its intelligence archives.

The former ADVENT infantry trooper hesitated when ordered to execute a wounded civilian during a pacification sweep. The refusal shattered the conditioning that had governed every movement. After killing two guards, the soldier escaped through a maintenance tunnel beneath the barracks, leaving behind a damaged neural implant. Days later, a Skirmisher patrol discovered the exhausted fugitive and brought them before Betos, who accepted their defection.

Assigned to reconnaissance, the former ADVENT soldier gradually noticed inconsistencies between implanted mission memories and the locations they surveyed. When a routine patrol uncovered an abandoned human settlement, suppressed memories resurfaced, overwhelming the conditioning. The soldier stole a transport vehicle from the installation motor pool and escaped during a shift change. After several days evading pursuit, they encountered Betos's Skirmishers and offered their knowledge of ADVENT patrol routes.

The former ADVENT heavy weapons operator regained independent thought when an ammunition explosion killed an entire squad, including soldiers whose final moments revealed unmistakable terror. Questioning the orders that had led them there, the soldier turned against the facility's command staff. A firefight left them with severe burns, but they escaped aboard a supply convoy. A Skirmisher patrol intercepted the vehicle and eventually secured their place among Betos's fighters.

Serving as an ADVENT military police officer, the soldier had spent years suppressing disturbances inside detention centers. Their conditioning weakened after discovering that prisoners scheduled for execution included individuals previously reported as deceased. The soldier secretly released several captives before escaping through the facility's evidence storage wing. Wounded by security personnel, they were rescued by former ADVENT defectors and eventually welcomed into Betos's Skirmisher faction.

The former ADVENT communications specialist experienced the first signs of independence while monitoring transmissions from a besieged civilian settlement. The desperate pleas contradicted everything the Elders had implanted about humanity's supposed gratitude. The soldier disabled the communications array, stole an access credential, and slipped out during the resulting confusion. After weeks of hiding in abandoned infrastructure, they located a Skirmisher safehouse and joined Betos's resistance.

An experimental medical procedure intended to strengthen neural obedience instead left the former ADVENT medic conscious of the conditioning embedded within their mind. Recognizing the procedure as another attempt to erase their remaining independence, the soldier sabotaged the laboratory's life-support systems. They escaped through an emergency evacuation corridor, suffering permanent damage to one eye. A Skirmisher reconnaissance team later recovered them and arranged an introduction to Betos.

The former ADVENT squad leader began questioning their orders after a subordinate repeatedly hesitated before firing on unarmed civilians. When the soldier attempted to intervene, the conditioning finally fractured under the conflicting commands. They led the squad away from its assigned route, then escaped alone when security forces surrounded them. Haunted by abandoning their soldiers, they eventually sought out Betos's faction, hoping to prevent others from suffering the same fate.

While assigned to an ADVENT training facility, the soldier experienced recurring memories of a childhood that supposedly never existed. The memories became impossible to suppress after encountering an old family photograph during a confiscated-property inspection. They escaped by impersonating an instructor during a facility evacuation, concealing their damaged identification implant beneath a uniform collar. A resistance contact eventually directed them to Betos's Skirmishers, where their training experience proved valuable.

The former ADVENT combat engineer discovered that demolition orders routinely concealed evidence of failed experiments beneath occupied settlements. Their conditioning weakened after finding human remains inside a sealed underground chamber. During the next scheduled inspection, the soldier planted charges against the facility's power infrastructure and escaped through a drainage system. Severe injuries forced them to seek medical assistance from a Skirmisher patrol, which brought them into Betos's faction.

An unexpected emotional response during the execution of captured resistance fighters disrupted the former ADVENT marksman's neural conditioning. The soldier lowered their rifle instead of completing the assigned operation, allowing several prisoners to escape before security forces intervened. Using their familiarity with elevated firing positions, they covered their own retreat from the compound. After surviving a prolonged pursuit, they were discovered by Betos's fighters and accepted into the Skirmishers.

The former ADVENT supply officer uncovered discrepancies between inventory records and shipments of human prisoners transported to an undisclosed research facility. Suspicion became independent thought when an intercepted manifest revealed their own designation among the scheduled experimental subjects. They concealed themselves inside a freight container and escaped during a nighttime delivery. A Skirmisher logistics operative eventually discovered the stowaway and arranged their recruitment into Betos's faction.

The soldier had served as an ADVENT vehicle operator, transporting troops between occupation checkpoints. Their conditioning broke during an ambush when a wounded passenger begged for help rather than issuing the usual automated commands. Unable to reconcile the request with their implanted loyalties, they drove away from the engagement and abandoned the transport. After hiding in a disused industrial complex, they encountered Skirmishers who recognized the value of their driving experience.

Assigned to guard an ADVENT detention block, the former soldier gradually became disturbed by prisoners who recognized them despite the conditioning suppressing all memories of their former lives. The decisive moment came when a captive addressed them using a childhood term of familiarity. The soldier opened several cells and escaped amid the resulting riot. Though pursued and badly injured, they reached Betos's resistance through assistance from another defector.

The former ADVENT marksman had never questioned an order until a routine overwatch assignment required eliminating a fleeing child. The soldier deliberately missed, exposing their position and triggering an immediate security response. After escaping across the facility's perimeter wall, they spent days surviving in hostile territory without communications or supplies. A Skirmisher scouting party eventually found them suffering from exposure and brought them into Betos's growing resistance.

An ADVENT laboratory technician assigned to weapons testing became increasingly disturbed by the neurological effects observed in captured soldiers. Their obedience deteriorated after witnessing a test subject retain consciousness while technicians attempted to erase their memories. The soldier sabotaged the laboratory's containment controls and escaped during the emergency response. Although their own implant remained partially functional, Betos's medical personnel eventually stabilized them and accepted their service.

The former ADVENT security officer had maintained strict discipline inside a military compound until an unexpected power failure exposed the brutality of its command structure. When officers began executing personnel accused of disloyalty, the soldier recognized the same fear they had witnessed among civilians. They escaped through an underground utility passage, abandoning their equipment and identification. A Skirmisher patrol later discovered them hiding beneath an abandoned transit station and recruited them.

The soldier served as an ADVENT combat medic, routinely treating wounded personnel before returning them to the battlefield. Their conditioning weakened after being ordered to leave a critically injured trooper untreated because the soldier's combat effectiveness had been deemed insufficient. Instead, the medic smuggled the patient out during a supply transfer. Both eventually escaped, but only the medic survived the journey to a Skirmisher outpost, where Betos's faction offered protection.

During an extended reconnaissance deployment, the former ADVENT soldier began experiencing independent thoughts whenever their squad entered abandoned human settlements. The discovery of personal belongings matching fragmented memories finally broke the conditioning. They falsified a patrol report, separated from the unit, and concealed themselves inside a collapsed apartment block. After evading several search teams, they encountered a Skirmisher courier and followed the resistance network to Betos.

The former ADVENT heavy weapons specialist had been conditioned to regard pain as irrelevant to mission completion. That certainty collapsed when an explosion destroyed their squad and left them trapped beneath collapsed concrete. Alone and conscious for hours, they began questioning the orders that had sent them there. After crawling through a damaged ventilation shaft, they escaped the installation and were later recovered by Betos's Skirmishers.

Assigned to military communications encryption, the soldier discovered an unauthorized transmission describing the systematic disposal of defective ADVENT personnel. Their own service record contained identical medical classifications. The revelation triggered a gradual collapse of their implanted obedience. They copied classified access codes, disabled the communications center, and escaped during the resulting lockdown. Betos's resistance eventually recruited them for their familiarity with ADVENT communication protocols.

The former ADVENT infantry soldier experienced a breakdown in conditioning after being forced to fight another unit during a fabricated disciplinary exercise. The opposing soldiers displayed the same confusion and fear that had begun troubling them. Rather than completing the engagement, they turned their weapon against the supervising officers. Escaping through the training grounds' underground firing range, they later encountered a Skirmisher patrol and joined Betos's faction.

A prolonged malfunction in the soldier's neural implant gradually restored fragments of suppressed memories, including memories of resisting the original ADVENT recruitment process. Their growing independence became dangerous when medical personnel scheduled an emergency procedure. They escaped the research facility by exploiting a ventilation maintenance route, leaving behind most of their equipment. After weeks of hiding, they were located by Betos's scouts and offered a place among the Skirmishers.

The former ADVENT facility guard had developed an unconscious habit of counting prisoners during transfers. One evening, the numbers failed to match the official records, revealing that several detainees had been secretly removed for experimentation. The discovery awakened suspicions that eventually overwhelmed their conditioning. They stole a security access card and escaped through the loading docks. A resistance operative later introduced them to Betos's faction.

Serving as a forward observer, the soldier coordinated ADVENT artillery strikes against resistance positions. Their conditioning fractured when inaccurate targeting data resulted in the destruction of a civilian shelter. Unable to suppress the memories of the victims, they deliberately transmitted false coordinates during the next operation. Security forces pursued them into a nearby industrial district, where a Skirmisher unit provided extraction and eventually secured their recruitment.

The former ADVENT squad support specialist had spent years maintaining equipment for soldiers whose identities remained hidden behind identical armor. Their independence emerged after a damaged helmet revealed the face of a fellow trooper who had died during an earlier deployment. Before joining the resistance, the soldier had worked as a municipal locksmith. ADVENT security installations gradually replaced civilian buildings throughout their district, and their technical experience made them useful to underground couriers. During one delivery, they discovered that an apparently abandoned apartment block concealed a detention facility. They began quietly opening restricted access points for prisoners and informants. Their activities eventually attracted Reaper attention, and they accepted recruitment after realizing the faction could provide better protection for their underground contacts.

The soldier had lived as a mountain shepherd, spending most of their life moving livestock between isolated pastures. When ADVENT established a communications relay near the settlement, livestock movements became restricted and unexplained disappearances increased. The soldier began using old grazing routes to move food beyond the surveillance perimeter. Their ability to recognize unfamiliar tracks helped expose an ADVENT patrol preparing to raid a nearby refuge. A Reaper team later recruited them as a guide through the surrounding mountains.

The soldier had worked as a crime-scene photographer before the occupation. Their experience documenting evidence became unexpectedly valuable after ADVENT began rewriting public records and concealing disappearances. They secretly photographed detention transports, damaged resistance safehouses, and military equipment shipments. When surveillance officers began questioning their movements, they abandoned their apartment and established a darkroom inside a condemned printing facility. A Reaper intelligence operative eventually acquired their photographs and arranged their recruitment as a field intelligence specialist.

The soldier had been a mechanic at a rural agricultural cooperative. Following ADVENT's introduction of automated farming systems, the cooperative lost its equipment and most of its workforce. The soldier survived by repairing abandoned machinery for isolated communities. They eventually discovered a damaged ADVENT transport vehicle containing tracking equipment intended for resistance infiltrators. Rather than sell the components, they dismantled the system and supplied the information to a nearby resistance cell. The Reapers later recruited them for their technical knowledge and practical approach to sabotage.

The soldier had worked as a wilderness search-and-rescue volunteer, locating missing hikers in difficult terrain. During the occupation, their rescue experience became a liability when ADVENT classified unauthorized movement between settlements as suspicious activity. They continued helping displaced civilians cross restricted territory, using weather patterns and terrain features to avoid patrols. After guiding several resistance couriers through an otherwise impassable mountain pass, they were approached by Reaper scouts and offered a position within the faction.

The soldier had been a professional burglar specializing in commercial properties. ADVENT surveillance made traditional theft increasingly dangerous, but their knowledge of building layouts and security weaknesses remained useful. They began stealing ration shipments from neglected distribution depots and leaving supplies at underground collection points. When a resistance contact disappeared, the soldier discovered that the network had been compromised by an informant. They abandoned their former criminal associates and eventually joined the Reapers, whose emphasis on secrecy suited their instincts.

The soldier had worked as a veterinary assistant in a small agricultural town. When ADVENT introduced compulsory livestock registration, they discovered that several farms were secretly being used to conceal experimental alien biological material. Refusing to cooperate, they began helping farmers move animals and supplies through disused drainage channels. Their knowledge of animal behavior also helped identify unfamiliar patrol activity around isolated properties. After providing valuable intelligence about the facility, they were recruited by Reaper operatives investigating the region.

The soldier had served as a border patrol officer before the invasion. Their former profession became meaningless when ADVENT dismantled national borders and replaced conventional checkpoints with occupation forces. They initially attempted to assist displaced civilians through official evacuation routes, only to discover that several transports were delivering passengers to detention centers. After abandoning their uniform, they began organizing unauthorized crossings through remote farmland. Their experience with surveillance procedures attracted the attention of the Reapers, who recruited them as a border reconnaissance specialist.

The soldier had maintained railway signaling equipment for a regional transport authority. ADVENT commandeered the network to move troops and supplies between controlled cities. Rather than sabotage the entire system, the soldier quietly introduced minor delays and false maintenance reports that disrupted military schedules. Their interference remained undetected for months until an inspection uncovered irregularities. Forced underground, they continued monitoring railway movements from abandoned signal huts. The Reapers eventually recruited them after receiving accurate intelligence about several ADVENT military transfers.

The soldier had grown up working in a family-owned greenhouse, developing extensive knowledge of soil, irrigation, and seasonal cultivation. ADVENT agricultural quotas eventually made independent farming illegal. When their community refused to surrender its remaining seed stores, the soldier concealed them inside an abandoned botanical research station. They learned to cultivate crops beneath artificial lighting while avoiding thermal detection from patrol drones. A Reaper supply operative discovered the hidden garden and recruited them to support remote faction safehouses.

The soldier had worked as a night-shift cleaner in a large metropolitan hospital. Their routine access to service corridors allowed them to observe ADVENT security procedures and the movement of detained civilians. After witnessing medical personnel falsify patient records to conceal unauthorized experiments, they began copying documents and passing them to resistance contacts. When hospital security identified the missing records, they escaped through a waste disposal tunnel. The Reapers later recruited them for their familiarity with controlled medical facilities.

The soldier had been a recreational climber who occasionally guided expeditions through abandoned industrial districts. After ADVENT fortified the city center, rooftops and maintenance structures became dangerous crossing points. The soldier adapted by using construction cranes, ventilation shafts, and damaged exterior walkways to move between buildings. They eventually became an unofficial courier for several isolated resistance groups. A Reaper scout noticed their movements during an intelligence operation and recruited them after confirming their ability to navigate heavily monitored urban terrain.

The soldier had operated a small roadside repair business, mostly servicing delivery vehicles and agricultural machinery. When ADVENT began inspecting civilian transport, their workshop became a useful source of information about occupation logistics. They quietly recorded vehicle numbers, delivery schedules, and unusual equipment modifications. After discovering that an ADVENT supply convoy carried components for a local surveillance network, they passed the information to resistance contacts. A Reaper intelligence team subsequently recruited them to help identify weaknesses in occupation transport systems.

The soldier had worked as a freshwater biologist studying river ecosystems. ADVENT industrial facilities eventually contaminated several waterways, forcing nearby communities to abandon traditional sources of drinking water. The soldier began mapping safe collection points and monitoring unusual chemical discharges. Their observations revealed a concealed disposal site connected to an alien research facility. They passed the findings through an underground medical network, attracting Reaper attention. Recruitment followed after they demonstrated an ability to gather intelligence without exposing the civilian communities they protected.

The soldier had been a former prison guard who lost their position when ADVENT replaced the local correctional system. Initially accepting employment under the occupation, they were assigned to monitor unauthorized detainees. After discovering that prisoners were being transferred without legal records, they began deliberately misdirecting security patrols. Eventually identified as unreliable, they escaped with several detainees and disappeared into the industrial outskirts. The Reapers approached them cautiously, recruiting them after verifying their knowledge of detention procedures.

The soldier had earned a living collecting scrap metal from abandoned construction sites. The occupation turned the work into a dangerous competition with ADVENT reclamation crews and automated security units. While dismantling a damaged transit station, they discovered an undocumented underground passage containing old resistance equipment. They used the passage to move supplies and establish several concealed storage locations. A Reaper team investigating the station found the network and recruited them for their resourcefulness and knowledge of urban ruins.

The soldier had worked as a rural schoolteacher before ADVENT imposed its standardized education system. Refusing to cooperate with occupation authorities, they began teaching displaced children in an unused agricultural storage building. Their lessons included practical navigation, identifying patrol insignia, and recognizing propaganda techniques. When security forces began questioning local families, the soldier relocated the classroom repeatedly. A Reaper operative eventually discovered the operation and recruited them, recognizing their ability to organize civilians without attracting unnecessary attention.

The soldier had been a demolition contractor specializing in clearing unstable buildings. Under ADVENT occupation, their expertise became useful to resistance groups seeking access through blocked infrastructure. However, after an ADVENT patrol sealed an underground shelter with survivors still inside, they began assisting evacuation efforts. Their careful knowledge of structural weaknesses allowed several communities to escape through concealed passages. The Reapers recruited them for their demolition expertise and measured approach to explosives.

The soldier had worked as a courier in a densely populated metropolitan district. Their job required memorizing streets, identifying shortcuts, and delivering packages without drawing attention. When ADVENT introduced movement restrictions, they began transporting messages for underground contacts alongside ordinary deliveries. One package contained evidence of a planned resistance roundup, allowing several safehouses to evacuate. Their courier network was eventually exposed, forcing them to disappear into the abandoned subway system. The Reapers recruited them after learning how effectively they had maintained communications under surveillance.

The soldier had been an amateur astronomer living in an isolated rural community. Their observation equipment initially seemed useless against the occupation, until they noticed irregular patterns in ADVENT aerial patrols. They began recording drone movements and predicting periods when settlements could move supplies unnoticed. Their findings eventually helped a resistance cell relocate an entire medical cache without detection. When ADVENT investigators searched their property, the soldier escaped with their observation records. Reaper intelligence personnel subsequently recruited them as a specialist in surveillance analysis.

The soldier had managed inventory for a large wholesale warehouse. After ADVENT took control of the distribution center, they were ordered to document shipments intended for military installations. They began manipulating stock records to conceal food and equipment diverted to civilian shelters. When an automated audit identified inconsistencies, they fled through the loading docks and established contact with underground traders. Their knowledge of occupation supply procedures proved valuable to the Reapers, who recruited them to identify vulnerabilities in ADVENT logistics.

The soldier had worked as a mountain rescue helicopter ground technician before the invasion. The soldier had been a former gang enforcer who understood intimidation better than cooperation. The Reapers recruited them after determining that their knowledge of criminal networks could expose several occupation collaborators.

The soldier had worked as a lighthouse keeper on a sparsely populated coastline. After ADVENT established an offshore monitoring station, civilian shipping was heavily restricted. The soldier had been a laboratory equipment technician specializing in precision instruments. The Reapers recruited them after verifying the intelligence and arranged their transfer to a concealed workshop.

The soldier had worked as a professional beekeeper in a rural agricultural region. ADVENT pesticide programs and compulsory land seizures threatened the remaining independent farms. When a resistance group needed someone capable of navigating the agricultural perimeter, the soldier volunteered. The soldier had worked as an antique dealer, specializing in recovering and restoring objects from abandoned properties. When a security investigation exposed the transactions, they fled with a collection of salvaged communications equipment. A Reaper quartermaster recruited them after learning of their extensive connections to the black market.

The soldier had been a former mountain infantry reservist who returned to civilian life before the invasion. Rather than enlist immediately, they taught local residents how to conceal food stores, maintain observation posts, and withdraw without leaving obvious trails. Their methods helped preserve several settlements through repeated patrol sweeps. The Reapers eventually approached them, recognizing their ability to organize survival networks without imposing conventional military structures.

The soldier had worked as a railway maintenance inspector in a region increasingly affected by Lost infestations. They began mapping safe passages for displaced civilians and identifying locations where the Lost congregated. After ADVENT patrols attempted to seal the network, they escaped through an old drainage junction. The soldier had been an independent scrap electronics dealer, buying damaged equipment and selling recovered components. After an inspection uncovered their activities, they escaped through an abandoned furnace complex. A Reaper operative later recruited them for their knowledge of industrial infiltration routes.

The soldier had been a professional falconer employed by a private wildlife sanctuary. Their knowledge of animal behavior helped them recognize disturbances caused by approaching patrols. They eventually began guiding resistance couriers through open countryside. A Reaper scout discovered their hidden refuge and recruited them as a field observer.

The soldier had worked as a meteorological observer at a remote mountain station. Their daily routine involved monitoring wind conditions, precipitation, and atmospheric disturbances. When occupation inspectors discovered missing stock, they fled through an abandoned drainage passage. The soldier had been a seasonal agricultural worker moving between large farms. Their life had involved repetitive labor, temporary accommodation, and little attachment to any particular settlement. Their ability to blend into civilian labor movements attracted Reaper attention, and they were recruited as an undercover observer.

The soldier had worked as a private security guard at a suburban shopping center. The soldier had been a cave exploration enthusiast who regularly surveyed underground passages.
