They began recovering discarded equipment from the seabed and discovered an abandoned pipeline connection leading beneath an occupation-controlled industrial complex. They mapped the route and passed the information to a resistance intelligence contact. The Reapers eventually recruited them to investigate submerged approaches and concealed infrastructure.

The soldier had worked as a secondhand electronics dealer in a crowded urban market. Their livelihood depended on repairing damaged devices and identifying useful components among discarded technology. When ADVENT restricted civilian electronics, they began dismantling occupation equipment recovered from abandoned vehicles. They discovered a recurring tracking component embedded in several apparently harmless communication devices. After warning nearby resistance groups, they relocated their workshop to a disused subway platform. The Reapers recruited them as a technical specialist in identifying surveillance equipment.

The soldier had been a former rural veterinarian who operated a mobile clinic serving scattered farming communities. ADVENT's livestock confiscations left many farmers without income or access to medical supplies. They began traveling between isolated properties under the pretense of treating animals while secretly distributing medicine and resistance intelligence. When an occupation patrol intercepted their vehicle, they abandoned their equipment and escaped through a wooded drainage corridor. The Reapers later recruited them for their regional contacts and ability to move discreetly between settlements.

The soldier had worked as a professional chimney sweep in an aging industrial city. Their occupation required entering buildings through rooftops and narrow maintenance spaces that ordinary inspectors rarely visited. When ADVENT began installing surveillance systems throughout residential districts, they noticed several camera networks shared the same blind spots around older buildings. They began mapping these areas and guiding underground couriers through them. After an occupation inspection exposed their unauthorized access, they disappeared into the city's abandoned industrial quarter. The Reapers recruited them as an urban infiltration guide.

The soldier had been a former agricultural machinery operator who worked seasonal harvests across several provinces. ADVENT's mechanized farming policies eventually eliminated most independent agricultural employment. They began repairing abandoned equipment for settlements that refused to cooperate with occupation authorities. Their improvised repairs kept several communities supplied with food despite repeated requisitions. When an ADVENT inspection team confiscated their workshop, they escaped with a collection of essential tools. A Reaper logistics operative eventually recruited them for their practical engineering abilities.

The soldier had worked as a professional archivist responsible for preserving municipal property records. ADVENT's occupation brought widespread destruction of historical documents and the disappearance of unofficial settlement records. They secretly copied maps showing abandoned service roads, forgotten shelters, and underground municipal infrastructure. When occupation administrators began auditing the archive, they hid the original documents in several separate locations. The Reapers eventually acquired copies through a resistance courier and recruited the soldier to maintain an independent archive of useful territorial intelligence.

The soldier had been a former ice-road transport driver working in a remote northern region. Their experience involved navigating frozen waterways and isolated roads under unpredictable weather conditions. ADVENT's occupation disrupted traditional supply routes, forcing them to develop alternative paths across abandoned mining areas. They began transporting medicine and equipment to settlements that had been cut off from official distribution. When a patrol discovered one of their supply caches, they relocated into the wilderness. The Reapers recruited them for their expertise in extreme-weather transportation.

The soldier had worked as a professional locksmith employed by a hotel maintenance company. After ADVENT requisitioned several large hotels for occupation administration, they were ordered to replace civilian access systems with military-controlled locks. They discovered that some occupied floors contained unauthorized detention rooms. Rather than complete the work, they began secretly disabling selected doors and helping prisoners communicate with outside contacts. Their actions were eventually noticed by security personnel. The Reapers recruited them after learning of their involvement in several successful escapes.

The soldier had been a former stage magician who earned a living performing at private events and small theaters. Their career had taught them how to manipulate attention, conceal objects, and recognize when someone was watching too closely. Under ADVENT, they used these abilities to exchange documents and small pieces of equipment in crowded public areas. When civilian gatherings were prohibited, they moved their activities to underground markets. A Reaper intelligence operative eventually recruited them for their discretion and ability to operate within heavily monitored civilian populations.

The soldier had worked as a mountain forestry technician responsible for maintaining firebreaks and monitoring tree disease. ADVENT's expansion into the region brought military construction crews into protected woodland. They noticed that several newly cleared areas concealed equipment storage sites rather than legitimate infrastructure projects. They began documenting the locations using forestry survey markers and passing the information to resistance scouts. When occupation patrols searched their station, they escaped into an abandoned logging district. The Reapers recruited them for their environmental knowledge and surveillance skills.

The soldier had been an independent mechanic repairing motorcycles and small engines. Their workshop became an important meeting point for local smugglers after ADVENT restricted civilian transportation. They began modifying vehicles to carry concealed supplies and operate with minimal electronic signatures. When a regular customer was exposed as an occupation informant, the soldier abandoned the business before the network was compromised. They later approached the Reapers after hearing reports of their operations and offered their mechanical expertise in exchange for protection.

The soldier had worked as a professional translator aboard international cargo vessels. Their language skills allowed them to communicate with crews from several countries and understand intercepted maritime broadcasts. When ADVENT assumed control of major shipping routes, they began collecting information about foreign vessels and unusual military shipments. Their reports revealed that several civilian ships were being redirected toward undisclosed detention facilities. The Reapers recruited them after receiving the intelligence through a coastal resistance network.

The soldier had been a former agricultural irrigation specialist working in a semi-arid region. ADVENT's seizure of the local water infrastructure threatened the survival of independent farming communities. They began repairing abandoned wells and constructing concealed water collection systems outside occupation-controlled distribution networks. Their knowledge of underground water sources allowed several settlements to survive prolonged restrictions. After an ADVENT patrol discovered one of the hidden reservoirs, they relocated into the surrounding badlands. The Reapers recruited them as a survival and logistics specialist.

The soldier had worked as a professional photographer specializing in architectural documentation. During the occupation, they were contracted to photograph buildings scheduled for demolition under ADVENT redevelopment programs. Their surveys revealed concealed rooms and access tunnels that were absent from official blueprints. They began secretly preserving the information for underground groups seeking shelter. After discovering that several buildings contained evidence of forced experimentation, they copied the records and disappeared. The Reapers recruited them for their ability to identify hidden structures and document occupation facilities.

The soldier had been a former security systems installer responsible for fitting alarms and electronic locks in commercial buildings. ADVENT later employed contractors with similar skills to expand its surveillance infrastructure. They accepted temporary work but quietly retained copies of outdated system configurations and maintenance codes. These records allowed resistance operatives to recognize weaknesses in several occupation installations. When their activities were discovered, they escaped through a commercial maintenance network. The Reapers recruited them as a technical infiltration specialist.

The soldier had worked as a rural grain mill operator in an agricultural settlement. When ADVENT imposed compulsory food requisitions, the mill became an important occupation-controlled distribution point. They began diverting small quantities of grain into concealed storage areas and providing food to unregistered families. Their operation survived several inspections because they maintained accurate official records while keeping a separate private inventory. Eventually, an occupation administrator noticed the discrepancy. The soldier fled and was later recruited by the Reapers to support isolated communities.

The soldier had been a former mountain bicycle racer who later worked as a wilderness guide. ADVENT's patrol network made conventional roads increasingly dangerous, but the soldier knew hundreds of unofficial trails connecting remote valleys. They began guiding resistance couriers through steep terrain and abandoned forestry tracks. After one patrol discovered their regular route, they developed a network of temporary caches and alternative crossings. A Reaper scouting party eventually recruited them for their speed, navigation skills, and ability to operate without vehicle support.

The soldier had worked as a commercial laundry delivery driver serving hospitals and residential complexes. Their routine deliveries provided access to buildings that had become difficult for ordinary civilians to enter. They noticed that several occupation facilities received unusually large quantities of medical laundry despite having no registered patient wards. They began recording delivery schedules and passed the information to underground contacts. After their vehicle was searched, they escaped into a nearby industrial district. The Reapers recruited them as an intelligence operative familiar with occupation medical facilities.

The soldier had been an ordinary caretaker at an abandoned military training ground. They maintained the property long after its original personnel had departed, gradually becoming familiar with its underground storage areas and forgotten equipment. ADVENT eventually occupied the surrounding region and used the site for patrol exercises. The soldier secretly recovered discarded training materials and supplied them to resistance volunteers. When the facility was placed under permanent military guard, they escaped through an old drainage tunnel. The Reapers recruited them for their knowledge of military infrastructure.

The soldier had worked as a professional taxidermist, preserving wildlife specimens for museums and private collectors. Their workshop contained specialized tools and storage materials that proved useful for repairing damaged field equipment. During the occupation, they began buying discarded clothing and disguising hidden supply containers as ordinary display objects. Their activities attracted attention after a black-market trader attempted to sell their workshop location to ADVENT. They escaped and eventually joined the Reapers, who valued their unusual craftsmanship and ability to improvise concealment.

The soldier had been a former river navigation officer responsible for marking hazards and maintaining shipping channels. ADVENT's control of regional waterways turned their knowledge into a valuable intelligence resource. They began recording patrol boat schedules and identifying stretches of water hidden from aerial surveillance. Their information helped resistance vessels transport equipment without using monitored ports. When occupation forces began questioning their survey records, they abandoned their official position. The Reapers recruited them as a specialist in riverine reconnaissance and transport.

The soldier had worked as a night watchman at a large abandoned shopping complex. Their responsibilities involved monitoring alarms, checking entrances, and preventing scavengers from damaging the property. When ADVENT began using the building as a temporary logistics depot, they noticed that security patrols ignored several underground maintenance areas. They began using those spaces to hide displaced civilians and store supplies. After a patrol discovered the shelter, they escaped through an old loading passage. The Reapers recruited them for their familiarity with commercial security layouts.

The soldier had been a former industrial chemist employed by a fertilizer manufacturer. ADVENT eventually requisitioned the facility and redirected its production toward military applications. They discovered that occupation technicians were experimenting with chemical compounds intended for use against resistance settlements. Rather than cooperate, they sabotaged the research records and escaped with technical documentation. They later passed the information to an underground intelligence network. The Reapers recruited them to assess chemical hazards and identify dangerous ADVENT research projects.

The soldier had worked as a remote telecommunications tower technician, maintaining antennas across sparsely populated regions. ADVENT's surveillance expansion turned many of these installations into military relay stations. They noticed that occupation engineers had left several older towers disconnected from the central network. They began using the abandoned equipment to establish temporary communications links between resistance communities. When security personnel traced an unauthorized transmission, they dismantled the system and moved into the countryside. The Reapers recruited them to maintain independent communication infrastructure.

The soldier had been a former professional stable hand working at a horse breeding facility. When ADVENT restricted independent animal ownership, the facility was converted into a military supply depot. They secretly preserved several horses and used them to transport equipment between rural settlements where vehicles attracted attention. Their familiarity with animal behavior helped them recognize approaching patrols before they reached the property. After the depot was searched, they fled with the remaining animals. The Reapers recruited them for their ability to support low-signature transportation.

The soldier had worked as a museum security guard before ADVENT occupied the city. Their job had involved protecting valuable collections and monitoring visitor behavior. When occupation authorities began removing historical artifacts and confiscating private archives, they started documenting the transfers. They discovered that several shipments contained more than cultural property, including confiscated civilian identification records. They copied the documentation and delivered it to resistance contacts. The Reapers recruited them for their familiarity with museum security and occupation seizure procedures.

The soldier had been a former professional roofer specializing in repairs to older residential buildings. Their work allowed them to move across rooftops and access buildings without entering through monitored streets. During the occupation, they began using these routes to deliver supplies to families hiding from registration patrols. Their knowledge of roof construction also helped identify unstable structures before couriers crossed them. After ADVENT security discovered several unauthorized rooftop passages, they escaped into an industrial district. The Reapers recruited them as an urban movement specialist.

The soldier had worked as a commercial livestock transporter moving animals between farms and processing facilities. ADVENT's agricultural seizure program made their work increasingly dangerous, as they witnessed unregistered farms being cleared. They began falsifying transport manifests to redirect animals toward independent settlements. When an occupation audit exposed the discrepancies, they escaped with a small transport vehicle and continued operating through back roads. A Reaper logistics operative eventually recruited them for their knowledge of rural transport networks and supply movement.

The soldier had been an amateur cave photographer who explored underground formations during their free time. The occupation forced them to abandon organized expeditions, but they continued investigating accessible cave systems. They discovered that an old natural cavern connected to a disused military storage facility. Inside, they found equipment that had been abandoned before ADVENT's arrival. They used the location as a temporary shelter and eventually guided resistance operatives through its passages. The Reapers recruited them as an underground reconnaissance specialist.

The soldier had worked as a commercial sign installer, fitting illuminated advertisements and business displays across a large city. ADVENT's propaganda campaign provided continuous employment, but they became increasingly disturbed by the messages they were ordered to install. They began altering selected signs to display coded warnings visible to resistance couriers. When occupation technicians noticed the irregularities, they abandoned their work vehicle and disappeared. The Reapers recruited them after learning that their coded displays had helped several underground groups coordinate movements without radio contact.

The soldier had been a former rural school bus driver responsible for transporting children between scattered villages. When ADVENT introduced compulsory education centers, several remote communities lost control over where their children were sent. They began secretly transporting families to unregistered settlements and using old agricultural roads to avoid checkpoints. After one journey was reported to occupation authorities, they abandoned their bus and continued on foot. The Reapers recruited them for their knowledge of rural roads and their commitment to protecting vulnerable civilians.

The soldier had worked as a commercial refrigeration inspector, checking food storage systems in supermarkets and distribution centers. ADVENT eventually commandeered the facilities and imposed strict inventory controls. They noticed that several storage rooms contained supplies absent from official records, including equipment for an undisclosed military research project. They copied the inventory data and passed it through a black-market contact. After an investigation began, they relocated to an abandoned warehouse. The Reapers recruited them for their ability to gather intelligence through routine industrial inspections.

The soldier had been a former professional tracker employed by a private search organization. Their work involved locating missing persons through footprints, disturbed vegetation, and environmental evidence. During the occupation, they began searching for civilians who disappeared during ADVENT registration operations. Several investigations revealed a pattern of unmarked transports moving through remote agricultural roads. They compiled the information and delivered it to resistance intelligence. The Reapers recruited them after recognizing their ability to reconstruct enemy movements from seemingly insignificant details.

The soldier had worked as an independent boatbuilder in a small coastal workshop. ADVENT's maritime restrictions destroyed most civilian demand for their services, but they continued repairing damaged fishing vessels for isolated communities. They began constructing small, quiet boats capable of navigating shallow waterways and concealed inlets. One of their vessels helped a resistance team evacuate a compromised safehouse. The Reapers later recruited them to support covert maritime operations and maintain small transport craft.

The soldier had been a former mining rescue volunteer familiar with underground emergency procedures. When ADVENT expanded its mining operations, several civilian workers disappeared following unexplained structural accidents. The soldier began investigating abandoned shafts and discovered that occupation authorities had sealed entire sections without proper evacuation records. They helped surviving workers escape through an older ventilation route. Their findings exposed an unauthorized underground facility. The Reapers recruited them for their experience navigating dangerous subterranean environments.

The soldier had worked as a freelance computer repair technician serving small businesses and private households. ADVENT's centralized identification system eventually made independent computer services suspicious. They began repairing obsolete equipment for resistance contacts, using disconnected machines to preserve information outside occupation networks. One damaged terminal contained fragments of an ADVENT surveillance database. They recovered enough information to identify several compromised safehouses before warning the resistance. The Reapers recruited them for their technical independence and ability to handle isolated computer systems.

The soldier had been a professional falconry assistant responsible for training and caring for hunting birds. After ADVENT restricted animal ownership, they relocated to an abandoned agricultural estate. They used their remaining birds to observe distant roads and identify approaching vehicles without electronic equipment. The method proved useful when automated surveillance drones began monitoring conventional resistance observation posts. A Reaper scout encountered the operation and recognized its value. The soldier was recruited as an unconventional reconnaissance specialist.

The soldier had worked as a professional cartographer producing commercial road and infrastructure maps. ADVENT's rapid construction projects and military restrictions made many pre-invasion maps unreliable. They began creating updated paper maps showing destroyed bridges, abandoned roads, patrol checkpoints, and accessible shelters. Their work circulated among independent resistance groups until an ADVENT search uncovered a copy. Forced to abandon their workshop, they continued mapping from temporary shelters. The Reapers recruited them to maintain accurate field maps of contested territory.

The soldier had been a former sanitation engineer responsible for maintaining underground waste treatment facilities. ADVENT's takeover of municipal infrastructure left many civilian districts dependent on poorly maintained systems. They discovered several forgotten service passages connecting residential blocks to industrial drainage networks. They began guiding resistance couriers through these passages and identifying areas suitable for concealed storage. When an occupation patrol sealed one entrance, they relocated the network. The Reapers recruited them for their knowledge of neglected underground infrastructure.

The soldier had worked as a rural hunting lodge cook, preparing meals for visitors and maintaining supplies during extended expeditions. After ADVENT restricted access to the surrounding forest, the lodge became a temporary refuge for displaced travelers. They began organizing food stores and teaching visitors how to preserve provisions without refrigeration. Their practical survival knowledge helped several families endure an extended winter blockade. A Reaper supply operative eventually discovered the shelter and recruited them to support remote faction camps.

The soldier had been a former commercial insurance photographer documenting damaged buildings and industrial accidents. During ADVENT's occupation, their work brought them into restricted areas where military construction had replaced civilian infrastructure. They began photographing concealed installations and recording details absent from official reports. One investigation revealed that a supposedly abandoned factory was operating as an alien equipment assembly site. After transmitting the images to resistance intelligence, they escaped the district. The Reapers recruited them as a photographic reconnaissance specialist.

The soldier had worked as a small-town butcher and meat supplier. When ADVENT introduced compulsory agricultural distribution, local food producers lost control of their inventories. They began secretly preserving meat and distributing it to households excluded from occupation ration systems. Their storage methods allowed food to remain usable without reliable electricity. After an ADVENT inspection discovered missing provisions, they escaped to a neighboring settlement. The Reapers recruited them for their practical supply knowledge and ability to sustain isolated resistance communities.

The soldier had been a former industrial maintenance supervisor responsible for overseeing repairs at a large manufacturing complex. ADVENT's military expansion transformed the facility into a production center for occupation equipment. They initially cooperated to protect the remaining civilian workforce, but eventually discovered that workers were being secretly monitored and removed. They began documenting personnel movements and arranging discreet departures for those at risk. When occupation security identified their involvement, they escaped through a maintenance access tunnel. The Reapers recruited them for their leadership, intelligence gathering, and knowledge of industrial operations.

The former lighthouse keeper had spent years maintaining an isolated coastal station after ADVENT consolidated control of the surrounding settlements. During a winter storm, they sensed an approaching patrol several minutes before its arrival, despite having no functioning communications equipment. Similar experiences followed, accompanied by an unsettling awareness of nearby minds. After investigating rumors of human psionic resistance, they sought out the Templars, hoping to understand what had awakened within them.

Once employed as a veterinary assistant, they had grown accustomed to treating injured animals in an overcrowded rural clinic. Their abilities first manifested when an injured animal became violently agitated near an ADVENT checkpoint. Without understanding how, they calmed it through an overwhelming wave of emotion. The experience left them exhausted but curious. A traveling Templar recognized their unusual sensitivity and offered an opportunity to develop it through disciplined training.

The former ADVENT communications technician had spent years monitoring encrypted transmissions and maintaining relay equipment. While repairing a damaged Psionic Network interface, they experienced a sudden intrusion of unfamiliar thoughts. Rather than receiving information through the equipment, they had somehow perceived the intentions of its operators. Disturbed by what the Elders had built, they abandoned their position and eventually approached the Templars, seeking knowledge beyond ADVENT's carefully controlled doctrine.

Before the occupation, they had worked as a professional carpenter in a small industrial town. Their awakening occurred when an unstable support beam collapsed inside an occupied workshop. Several heavy objects shifted unexpectedly, creating enough clearance for trapped workers to escape. They initially attributed the incident to structural movement, but subsequent accidents revealed otherwise. A Templar patrol investigating the settlement discovered their abilities and offered them sanctuary and training.

The former schoolteacher had continued educating children under ADVENT supervision, quietly preserving forbidden human history in discarded textbooks. During an inspection, they sensed the fear of every child in the classroom simultaneously. The emotional pressure became unbearable, and an unexplained mental disturbance forced the inspecting officer to withdraw. Fearing further incidents, they left the settlement. A resistance contact eventually introduced them to the Templars, whose teachings offered an alternative to ADVENT's control.

They had served as a commercial fisherman before occupation forces restricted access to the surrounding waters. During an extended voyage, they began sensing living creatures beneath the surface without seeing them. Initially dismissed as exhaustion, the sensations became increasingly precise. One night, they located a missing crew member through an inexplicable mental connection. After returning to shore, they followed rumors of individuals capable of understanding such phenomena and eventually joined the Templars.

The former military medic had treated casualties throughout several years of resistance operations. Their abilities emerged during an evacuation when a wounded operative stopped breathing. As they worked desperately to revive the patient, they experienced the dying person's memories and emotions with disturbing clarity. The connection vanished when the patient survived. Uncertain whether the experience could be repeated, they accepted an invitation from a Templar initiate to investigate their potential.

Before the occupation, they had worked nights as a railway signal operator. Their awakening began with recurring impressions of approaching danger, often arriving seconds before warning lights activated. During an ADVENT transport accident, these instincts allowed several passengers to escape before the damaged carriage collapsed. Investigators could find no explanation for their unusually precise reactions. A Templar scout later encountered them while searching the wreckage and arranged their introduction to the faction.

The former museum conservator had spent much of their career restoring damaged historical artifacts. While examining an alien object recovered from an abandoned research facility, they experienced unfamiliar memories that seemed to originate from the material itself. Repeated exposure produced headaches and fragmented impressions of distant voices. Rather than surrender the discovery to ADVENT authorities, they concealed their findings. Eventually, they sought the Templars, believing their abilities might reveal what conventional research could not.

They had lived quietly as a baker in a settlement largely untouched by resistance activity. Their first manifestation occurred during an ADVENT raid, when a frightened child became trapped beneath overturned furniture. Without conscious effort, they sensed the child's position through the surrounding panic and directed rescuers toward the correct building. The incident attracted unwanted attention. A passing resistance operative helped them escape and introduced them to the Templars.

Formerly employed as a geological surveyor, they had spent years studying underground formations and abandoned mining sites. During an expedition beneath an ADVENT-controlled industrial district, they began detecting faint mental impressions from living beings through solid rock. The sensations became stronger near groups of people. Initially convinced that environmental conditions were affecting their judgment, they eventually accepted that their perception had changed. They joined the Templars after discovering their sanctuary through a resistance expedition.

They had worked as a prison transport officer under the ADVENT administration, gradually becoming uncomfortable with the disappearances of detainees. Their abilities manifested when they unexpectedly heard the thoughts of a prisoner during interrogation. The experience exposed fragments of memories concerning secret Psionic Network experiments. Unable to ignore what they had learned, they deserted their position. The Templars accepted them after they demonstrated an unusual resistance to external psionic influence.

Before the occupation, they had been an amateur astronomer who spent evenings recording celestial observations from a rural observatory. Their awakening came through increasingly vivid dreams in which distant human voices appeared to overlap. During one particularly intense episode, they accurately identified the presence of several hidden resistance operatives outside the settlement. Intrigued rather than frightened, they investigated rumors of the Templars and eventually requested admission to their order.

The former emergency dispatcher had spent years coordinating rescue operations during natural disasters. Their abilities emerged gradually through an unexplained sensitivity to distress, allowing them to distinguish individual voices within crowded communications channels. During an ADVENT bombardment, they began identifying survivors without receiving any transmissions. Their employers considered the reports impossible. After escaping the occupied district, they encountered a Templar recruitment party and recognized an opportunity to understand their unusual perception.

They had once maintained agricultural machinery on a remote communal farm. Their life changed when an ADVENT inspection resulted in the detention of several workers. Watching the frightened group being transported away, they experienced a sudden pressure that disrupted nearby electronic equipment. The effect lasted only seconds, but it attracted the attention of the authorities. A resistance group helped them disappear, eventually directing them toward Templar training.

The former laboratory assistant had worked on neurological research before ADVENT reorganized the institution into a facility studying human compatibility with alien technology. While examining experimental brain scans, they noticed activity patterns resembling their own recurring dreams. An accidental mental connection with a test subject confirmed their suspicions. Horrified by the experiments, they escaped with stolen research data and later joined the Templars to pursue a less exploitative understanding of psionic potential.

They had been a professional stage magician before the occupation, earning a modest living through misdirection and mechanical illusions. Their abilities first appeared during a performance when several concealed objects moved without physical contact. They initially suspected faulty equipment, but repeated incidents made that explanation impossible. Rather than viewing the experience as a supernatural gift, they approached it as a skill requiring experimentation. The Templars eventually offered the discipline they had been seeking.

The former border patrol officer had spent years monitoring isolated settlements vulnerable to ADVENT raids. During an overnight watch, they became aware of an approaching patrol despite the absence of movement or sound. Their warning saved the settlement from a surprise attack. Subsequent incidents revealed an ability to sense hostile intentions at considerable distances. A Templar scout investigating the raid recognized the potential and invited them to undertake formal training.

They had worked as a laundress in an overcrowded urban district, living an otherwise unremarkable life beneath ADVENT occupation. Their awakening was neither violent nor dramatic. They gradually discovered that nearby people's strongest memories sometimes surfaced in their mind as brief, involuntary impressions. The experience made ordinary social interactions increasingly difficult. After learning about the Templars from a displaced civilian, they sought the faction's assistance in establishing mental boundaries.

Once employed as an industrial electrician, they had spent years repairing power distribution systems across several ADVENT-controlled facilities. During a major blackout, they experienced an inexplicable connection with the electrical infrastructure, sensing faults before instruments registered them. The phenomenon later extended beyond machinery to nearby living minds. Unwilling to become another ADVENT research subject, they deserted and eventually joined the Templars, whose approach emphasized personal mastery rather than exploitation.

The former wilderness guide had helped refugees cross remote mountain regions while avoiding ADVENT patrols. During one winter crossing, they became separated from their group in a blizzard. Despite poor visibility, they sensed the presence of the missing refugees and led rescuers directly to them. They could offer no rational explanation for their certainty. After delivering the survivors to safety, they accepted an invitation to accompany the Templars and investigate their unusual awareness.

They had been an accountant before ADVENT occupation disrupted civilian employment. Their awakening occurred during an ordinary evening spent reviewing old financial records. Numbers began appearing in their thoughts before they consciously read them, accompanied by unfamiliar impressions of nearby individuals. The phenomenon intensified until they could barely distinguish their own thoughts from others'. A Templar initiate encountered them while investigating reports of unusual civilian behavior and arranged an introduction to the faction.

The former demolition specialist had worked with resistance cells sabotaging ADVENT supply routes. During an operation inside an abandoned transport depot, an unexpected explosion trapped them beneath structural debris. As panic set in, they unconsciously held several tons of collapsing material away from their body long enough for rescuers to reach them. The manifestation left them physically exhausted. Their surviving comrades later arranged contact with the Templars, where they sought greater control over the dangerous ability.

They had served as a caretaker at a small rural cemetery, maintaining grounds abandoned by most local authorities. Their abilities emerged after they began experiencing memories belonging to visitors who had recently passed through the grounds. The impressions were fragmented but emotionally intense. Concerned about their deteriorating concentration, they sought medical assistance, only to discover similar reports connected to unexplained neurological activity. A Templar traveler eventually offered them a place among others with comparable experiences.

Before joining the resistance, they had worked as a commercial photographer documenting ordinary life under occupation. Their awakening occurred while photographing an ADVENT procession. Through the camera lens, they suddenly perceived the emotional states of the surrounding crowd as distinct mental impressions. The experience exposed concealed hostility among seemingly compliant civilians. They began using their sensitivity to identify informants and eventually attracted the attention of Templar operatives, who offered specialized training.

They had been a rural pharmacist, distributing essential medicines through settlements increasingly neglected by ADVENT authorities. During an epidemic, they began sensing which patients were approaching a critical condition before their symptoms became apparent. The ability was inconsistent and offered no direct medical knowledge, but it saved several lives. After an ADVENT inspection threatened to expose their unusual observations, they fled with a group of refugees and eventually joined the Templars.

The former naval engineer had spent years maintaining obsolete vessels after conventional maritime transport collapsed. Their first manifestation occurred during an underwater repair operation, when they sensed another diver's distress before receiving an emergency signal. The sensation developed into an ability to establish brief mental connections with nearby individuals. Fascinated by the phenomenon, they began researching human psionic potential. A Templar expedition eventually recruited them after hearing about their unusual experiences.

They had worked as a municipal sanitation inspector before ADVENT occupation made their position largely ceremonial. While investigating an abandoned residential complex, they discovered an injured resistance operative hiding beneath the building. Without understanding how, they communicated reassurance directly into the operative's mind. The connection lasted only moments but established a new possibility. They later sought the Templars independently, believing humanity needed to understand abilities that had previously seemed impossible.

The former ADVENT medical orderly had assisted in transferring patients between neurological examination facilities. Repeated exposure to Psionic Network equipment produced unexplained headaches and recurring sensations of another consciousness observing them. During one transfer, they instinctively disrupted a nearby Psi Operative's concentration. The incident prompted an investigation, forcing them to flee before ADVENT could examine their brain activity. The Templars eventually accepted them as a promising but inexperienced initiate.

They had spent much of their life repairing clocks and precision instruments in a small workshop. Their abilities first appeared when several delicate mechanisms began moving simultaneously without being touched. Initially convinced that electromagnetic interference was responsible, they conducted increasingly elaborate tests. Eventually, they demonstrated limited control over small objects through concentration alone. Their experiments attracted a resistance researcher who introduced them to the Templars, where their mechanical patience proved useful during training.

They had worked as a midwife in a remote settlement, assisting families who had little access to medical facilities. Their awakening occurred during a difficult delivery when they suddenly experienced the unborn child's distress as an overwhelming mental impression. The sensation guided their actions until the emergency passed. Uncertain whether the experience was psychological or something else, they eventually sought the Templars after hearing reports of individuals who could perceive life beyond ordinary senses.

The former mining supervisor had spent years managing workers beneath an isolated industrial settlement. During a cave-in, they sensed several trapped miners through the surrounding rock, although rescue instruments indicated no survivors. Their insistence led rescuers to a concealed chamber where the missing workers remained alive. The experience changed their understanding of perception. After the mine was seized by ADVENT, they escaped and joined a Templar scouting party searching the region.

They had been a traveling street vendor, moving between settlements and trading whatever goods remained available. Their awakening developed through repeated encounters with strangers whose intentions they seemed to recognize immediately. The impressions were sometimes wrong, making them distrust their own judgment. During a confrontation with ADVENT security, they sensed an attack moments before it happened. A nearby resistance operative later helped them locate the Templars, where they hoped to distinguish instinct from genuine psionic perception.

The former forensic technician had assisted civilian investigators before ADVENT dismantled independent law enforcement. While examining evidence from an unexplained death, they experienced a sudden mental impression of the victim's final moments. Subsequent incidents suggested that intense emotional traces could trigger similar experiences. Troubled by the possibility that their mind was absorbing information involuntarily, they sought out the Templars and accepted their demanding methods of mental discipline.

They had lived as a shepherd in an isolated agricultural community, spending most days alone with livestock. Their awakening began when the animals repeatedly reacted to dangers before any physical threat became visible. Eventually, they discovered that the warnings originated from their own awareness of nearby living minds. When ADVENT patrols approached the settlement, their warning allowed the community to evacuate. A resistance contact later arranged their introduction to the Templars.

Before the occupation, they had worked as a professional chef in a busy urban restaurant. Their abilities first manifested during a crowded evening when an argument escalated into violence. They suddenly perceived the emotions of everyone nearby, distinguishing fear, anger, and impending aggression with overwhelming clarity. The experience caused them to abandon their profession temporarily. After several months of isolation, they encountered a Templar operative who helped them find purpose through controlled psionic training.

The former ADVENT security analyst had spent years evaluating reports of resistance activity and identifying potential insurgents. While examining recordings of a captured Templar, they experienced a powerful mental intrusion that revealed fragments of another person's memories. Their subsequent attempts to understand the phenomenon exposed their own unusual neurological activity. Increasingly distrustful of ADVENT's treatment of psionic individuals, they defected and eventually sought membership in the Templar order.

They had been a forest ranger responsible for protecting wildlife reserves from illegal exploitation. During an ADVENT sweep through the region, they became aware of frightened animals fleeing through distant woodland. The impressions arrived as vague emotional signals rather than recognizable thoughts. Later, they learned to distinguish individual living presences with increasing accuracy. A Templar patrol encountered them while investigating an abandoned checkpoint and offered an opportunity to develop their sensitivity.

The former radio repairman had maintained civilian communication equipment throughout the occupation. One evening, while testing a damaged receiver, they heard a voice that was not transmitted through any recognizable frequency. The message contained fragments of a stranger's thoughts, accompanied by sensations of distance and fear. Subsequent experiments revealed an unstable ability to establish mental contact. It was subsequently assigned to technical support operations where its strength proved useful for clearing obstructions.

The SPARK's first operational assignment involved supporting a squad tasked with destroying an ADVENT communications installation. Following the operation, its targeting systems were adjusted to improve coordination with nearby infantry units.

Assembled under pressure following a series of unsuccessful resistance engagements, this SPARK received only essential modifications before deployment. This unit spent its first weeks in reserve while Shen investigated irregularities in its movement controls. Its operators noted that it consistently maintained a position between casualties and approaching enemy forces.

The SPARK was assembled from components recovered during an XCOM supply operation. Its original power system was replaced with a more reliable configuration before activation. Assigned to support infantry advances, it became particularly effective at suppressing ADVENT troops occupying elevated defensive positions.

During an operation against an ADVENT ammunition depot, the SPARK sustained damage that disabled its primary weapon. Rather than withdraw, it continued supporting the squad by occupying an exposed approach and drawing enemy fire. Engineers later restored the weapon system and reinforced its damaged armor.

This SPARK was built using standard engineering procedures and passed activation testing without incident. Its service record is notable mainly for consistency. Across numerous assignments, it maintained reliable performance in direct assaults, defensive operations, and emergency extractions, requiring little beyond routine maintenance.

Constructed to support operations in heavily contaminated areas, the SPARK received additional environmental sealing before activation. Its equipment proved useful during missions involving damaged industrial facilities. The unit's maintenance schedule was subsequently revised after repeated exposure to corrosive substances affected its external connectors.

Engineers adjusted its stabilization systems following several early deployments. The modification improved its performance, and it subsequently became a reliable asset during mobile assaults against ADVENT positions.

Assigned to accompany Templar operations, this SPARK provided conventional fire support while the Templars engaged enemy forces at close range. Its targeting systems were adjusted to account for rapidly changing friendly positions. This unit was constructed with reinforced mobility components after engineers identified weaknesses in earlier chassis configurations. It was regularly deployed to battlefields containing rubble, damaged roads, and collapsed structures. The squad adjusted its position to compensate, allowing the operation to continue. Shen later corrected the targeting parameters and introduced additional battlefield diagnostics.

Although the mount required frequent lubrication, its combat performance justified the additional maintenance burden.

Recovered from a battlefield after an extraction operation, this SPARK was initially considered beyond repair. Engineers discovered that its central processing systems remained intact despite extensive external damage. Following reconstruction, it returned to service and was assigned to missions requiring dependable heavy weapons support.

The SPARK subsequently demonstrated improved responsiveness while retaining its methodical approach to defensive engagements.

This SPARK was assembled from parts accumulated during several successful resistance supply raids. Its construction took longer than expected because compatible components were scarce. Once completed, it was assigned to support operations against ADVENT patrols, where its heavy weapons provided an effective alternative to limited infantry ammunition.

This SPARK was assembled using components recovered from an abandoned XCOM supply cache. Its original movement controls were incompatible with the available chassis, requiring several adjustments before activation. Once operational, it was assigned to escort missions and proved particularly effective at protecting supply personnel during contested resupply operations.

The unit was constructed with reinforced shoulder assemblies after engineers identified excessive strain caused by its heavy weapons configuration. Its first deployments involved assaults against ADVENT defensive positions. The improved structure performed as intended, although technicians continued monitoring the assemblies for signs of fatigue.

During an operation to disable an ADVENT surveillance installation, the SPARK discovered that its standard targeting systems were unable to distinguish several concealed automated defenses. It switched to manual target acquisition and continued supporting the squad. Its software was subsequently updated to improve recognition of concealed mechanical threats.

This SPARK was assembled as a standard replacement unit after XCOM's existing mechanical forces suffered significant operational losses. Its construction required no unusual procedures, and it entered service following routine testing. It became a dependable addition to assault squads, particularly those assigned to destroy ADVENT communications infrastructure.

The unit received an improved lower chassis after its original suspension repeatedly failed during operations in mountainous terrain. Shen authorized the replacement of several mechanical assemblies with stronger components. The modification increased its operational weight but significantly reduced mobility failures during subsequent deployments.

Assigned to support Templar operations, this SPARK was configured to provide covering fire rather than participate in close engagements. Its targeting systems were adjusted to account for rapidly changing friendly positions. The arrangement proved effective, particularly when Templar forces advanced against fortified ADVENT defenders.

This SPARK was constructed using an incomplete chassis recovered during a resistance salvage operation. Engineers manufactured replacement structural components and adapted its power distribution system to the available equipment. After an extended evaluation, it entered service as a general-purpose combat unit with no significant operational restrictions.

During its first engagement with an ADVENT MEC, the SPARK's targeting system repeatedly failed to account for the enemy's reinforced armor. The squad compensated by concentrating fire on exposed mechanical joints. Engineers later modified its targeting parameters, improving its effectiveness against heavily armored robotic enemies.

The unit was originally assembled for defensive assignments but was later transferred to mobile assault operations following a shortage of frontline support. Its armor configuration proved adequate for both roles. Several commanders subsequently requested its inclusion in mixed squads because of its ability to adapt without additional modifications.

An inspection revealed that the SPARK's internal cooling system had been assembled using a component with insufficient capacity. Shen ordered its replacement before the machine could be deployed. The resulting unit operated reliably during extended firefights and became a regular choice for missions involving sustained heavy weapons use.

This SPARK accompanied an XCOM squad tasked with securing an abandoned ADVENT vehicle depot. Its primary responsibility was to clear obstructed access routes and protect the recovery team. It successfully moved several damaged vehicles away from the installation entrance, allowing engineers to recover valuable mechanical components.

Constructed to operate alongside inexperienced resistance fighters, the SPARK received simplified communications protocols and improved friendly identification systems. Its ability to maintain coordinated fire without extensive operator intervention made it useful during training operations and missions involving newly recruited personnel.

The machine's first deployment was interrupted when an enemy explosive device damaged its primary movement controller. It remained operational but could no longer maintain normal mobility. After recovery, engineers installed a replacement controller and additional protective shielding. The SPARK subsequently returned to active service without recurring problems.

This unit was built with a specialized weapon configuration intended to neutralize ADVENT automated turrets. Its targeting software emphasized mechanical vulnerabilities rather than conventional infantry threat assessment. Following several successful operations, it was occasionally assigned to broader combat missions where its specialized equipment remained effective.

The SPARK was assembled from a standard chassis that had previously been reserved for engineering evaluations. After receiving its combat systems, it passed all activation tests and entered service. Its operational history was distinguished by consistent performance during missions involving the defense of exposed extraction points.

During an operation in a damaged industrial district, the SPARK identified a structural weakness in an elevated firing position occupied by ADVENT troops. Its heavy weapons brought down part of the structure, forcing the defenders to abandon their position. The incident prompted engineers to review its environmental targeting capabilities.

This SPARK received additional armor around its central processing compartment after an earlier unit was disabled by a precision strike. The modification required extensive internal rearrangement but did not affect its overall performance. It subsequently served in high-risk assaults where protecting critical systems was considered essential.

The unit was constructed using recovered components from an ADVENT maintenance facility. Several mechanical assemblies were compatible with XCOM equipment, although their control systems required substantial modification. After Tygan completed his inspection, the SPARK was approved for service and assigned to operations against enemy robotic forces.

This machine was regularly deployed with squads responsible for protecting XCOM's forward supply positions. Its primary task was to discourage ADVENT attacks and provide immediate support when enemy patrols approached. Its consistent performance allowed commanders to reduce the number of soldiers assigned to static defensive duties.

A damaged weapon stabilizer caused this SPARK to produce inaccurate fire during its first operational evaluation. Rather than replace the entire assembly, Shen authorized a revised stabilization mechanism. The repaired unit passed subsequent testing and was assigned to missions requiring accurate fire against fortified enemy positions.

Constructed with a modified power distribution network, this SPARK was designed to support additional electronic equipment without compromising its combat systems. It was assigned to technical recovery teams operating near ADVENT installations. Its ability to carry and operate supplementary equipment proved valuable during several intelligence recovery missions.

The SPARK's service history includes repeated assignments to squads conducting operations in heavily wooded regions. Its sensors were modified to compensate for restricted visibility, while its movement systems received additional protection against branches and debris. The resulting configuration proved reliable during extended patrols through difficult terrain.

This unit was recovered after being immobilized during an unsuccessful resistance assault. Its movement systems had suffered extensive damage, but its weapon controls remained functional. Engineers rebuilt the lower chassis and returned it to combat duty. Its subsequent assignments emphasized stationary fire support rather than rapid movement.

The SPARK was assembled to provide additional protection during operations involving the recovery of captured resistance intelligence. Its heavy armor allowed it to remain exposed while human personnel searched dangerous locations. Following several successful missions, it became a preferred assignment for operations requiring prolonged security around sensitive equipment.

Early battlefield reports indicated that the unit consistently delayed movement until nearby infantry had reached designated positions. Engineers initially suspected a communications problem, but further examination revealed that its coordination software was applying outdated movement priorities. Following correction, the SPARK retained its deliberate positioning behavior without delaying squad advances.

This SPARK was constructed during an expansion of XCOM's available engineering capacity. Its assembly followed standard procedures, although several components were sourced from salvaged equipment. It passed all operational checks and was assigned to support infantry advances against ADVENT checkpoints and fortified patrol positions.

During an engagement inside an ADVENT-controlled transportation hub, the SPARK sustained damage to its sensor array from an explosive blast. Its targeting capabilities were reduced, but it continued operating through direct squad coordination. Replacement sensors were installed after the mission, along with additional protection against explosive fragmentation.

The unit was specifically configured for operations involving the protection of XCOM technical specialists. Its movement protocols prioritized maintaining access to evacuation routes and securing nearby machinery. It completed several recovery assignments without losing protected equipment, establishing a reputation for reliable defensive support.

This SPARK received a modified weapon cooling assembly after repeated deployments revealed overheating during prolonged suppression. The upgrade reduced the time required between sustained firing sequences. It was subsequently assigned to operations against fortified ADVENT positions, where continuous weapons support was frequently required.

Constructed using an older chassis design, this SPARK was expected to serve primarily as a reserve unit. However, its initial combat evaluations revealed excellent mechanical reliability. It was quickly promoted to regular operational status and became a common assignment for squads conducting routine resistance raids.

The SPARK was deployed alongside a squad tasked with securing an ADVENT-controlled medical facility. During the engagement, it maintained a defensive position near the extraction area while soldiers recovered medical supplies. Its armor sustained several direct impacts, but its weapon systems remained operational throughout the withdrawal.

Engineers modified this unit's movement programming after repeated observations showed difficulty navigating narrow interior passages. The revised system improved turning accuracy and obstacle detection. Its subsequent assignments focused on clearing buildings and underground facilities, where the improved maneuverability offered a clear operational advantage.

This SPARK was assembled using components recovered from a destroyed resistance transport. Although its external armor was beyond repair, several internal mechanical systems remained functional. The rebuilt machine passed activation testing and was assigned to general combat support, where its relatively simple configuration made it easy to maintain.

The unit was assigned to support Reaper operations against an ADVENT supply installation. Its heavy weapons were reserved for situations in which concealed resistance fighters encountered unexpected enemy resistance. The arrangement proved effective, allowing the Reapers to retain their preferred approach while maintaining access to reliable emergency fire support.

During an extended mission, the SPARK's power regulator began producing irregular output. The machine automatically reduced nonessential system activity and continued operating until extraction. Shen later approved replacement of the regulator and introduced additional monitoring procedures to identify similar faults before future deployments.

This unit was constructed to provide reliable fire support during resistance operations involving multiple enemy positions. Its targeting system was configured to maintain awareness of several threats simultaneously. The SPARK demonstrated consistent performance during coordinated infantry advances and was frequently assigned to squads operating without dedicated heavy weapons specialists.

The SPARK's initial configuration included an experimental movement sensor that proved unreliable under heavy electromagnetic interference. After several unsuccessful attempts to correct the problem, Shen ordered its removal and installed a conventional replacement. The simplified system proved substantially more dependable during operations near ADVENT technology.

Assembled from standard XCOM components, this SPARK received additional reinforcement around its weapon mounting points before activation. It was intended to support repeated assaults against defensive structures. Its service record includes numerous engagements in which it continued firing despite sustaining significant damage to its external armor.

This machine was assigned to protect resistance engineers repairing a damaged communications relay. When ADVENT forces attacked the work site, the SPARK moved to block their approach and maintained suppression until the repairs were completed. The unit subsequently received improved defensive positioning routines.

The SPARK's first several missions revealed a tendency to conserve ammunition even when additional suppression would have been tactically useful. Engineers adjusted its firing priorities following a review of combat recordings. The revised programming produced a more balanced approach without significantly increasing ammunition consumption.

This unit was assembled with additional protection for its lower power connections after engineers identified a vulnerability during environmental testing. Its first assignments involved operations in areas with unstable electrical infrastructure. The modification proved effective, and the SPARK completed several missions without suffering power interruptions.

During an assault on an ADVENT-controlled manufacturing facility, the SPARK became trapped behind a collapsed section of industrial machinery. Its manipulators cleared enough debris to restore a usable route, allowing it to rejoin the squad. Engineers subsequently expanded its obstacle assessment routines for similar environments.

Constructed as an emergency replacement during a period of heavy operational losses, this SPARK entered service after an accelerated evaluation. Its configuration emphasized durability and ease of repair rather than specialized combat capabilities. It performed reliably across multiple assignments and became an important part of XCOM's reserve mechanical force.

The unit was frequently assigned to operations involving the destruction of ADVENT defensive emplacements. Its targeting systems were calibrated to identify structural weaknesses, while its weapon mount was reinforced for repeated heavy firing. Several successful assaults demonstrated the effectiveness of the configuration, although maintenance requirements remained substantial.

Recovered during a resistance salvage operation, the SPARK had suffered damage to its central processing compartment. Engineers replaced the affected systems and rebuilt its external armor using available materials. After activation, it was assigned to reserve duty until repeated evaluations confirmed that its restored systems were reliable.

This SPARK was configured to operate as a mobile defensive platform during operations involving exposed supply drops. Its tactical routines emphasized covering approaches and maintaining clear lines of retreat. It became a regular assignment for squads tasked with recovering supplies from areas under frequent ADVENT patrol activity.

The machine was constructed with an upgraded sensor package intended to improve target recognition at extended distances. During its first deployment, it identified an approaching ADVENT patrol before the squad's other equipment detected the threat. Its early warning allowed XCOM personnel to establish an advantageous defensive position.

This unit was assigned to support operations conducted alongside Skirmisher forces attempting to disrupt ADVENT supply networks. Its heavy weapons provided covering fire during rapid assaults, while its armor allowed it to remain exposed during withdrawal. Its mobility controls were later adjusted to better accommodate the Skirmishers' unpredictable movement patterns.

A routine inspection discovered abnormal wear in the SPARK's weapon elevation mechanism. Although the unit remained fully operational, Shen ordered the component replaced before further deployment. The revised assembly improved targeting stability, and the machine returned to service with no significant reduction in combat readiness.

The SPARK was assembled using a combination of newly manufactured components and machinery recovered from an ADVENT-controlled depot. Its unusual configuration required additional testing by Tygan and Shen before approval. Once deployed, it proved especially effective against automated defenses and became a regular part of XCOM's technical assault teams.
